questions.explanation: By statute, a Colorado broker is presumed to be a transaction-broker unless single agency is established by a written agreement, and the listing form itself says the broker works with the seller as a transaction-broker if neither box is checked. An unchecked box doesn't void the contract or create agency.

questions.stem: A listing contract includes a holdover clause. After the listing expires, the seller sells to a buyer the broker had shown the house to. For the holdover clause to apply under Commission rules, the broker must have:
choices: given the seller that buyer's name in writing during the listing term
recorded the listing contract with the county clerk and recorder
kept the sign in the yard throughout the holdover period
notified the Commission in writing of each prospect shown during the term
questions.explanation: Holdover clauses may cover only persons the broker negotiated with during the listing whose names were given to the client in writing during the listing term.

questions.stem: A purchase contract is mutually executed on Monday. The listing brokerage, named earnest money holder, receives the buyer's check on Tuesday. Assuming no holidays, the brokerage must deposit it by the end of:
choices: Wednesday
Thursday
Friday
the following Tuesday
questions.explanation: Earnest money held by a firm must be deposited within 3 business days after receipt or mutual execution, whichever is later. The later event is Tuesday, so the deadline is Friday.

questions.stem: A property management firm receives a tenant's security deposit. Within what time must it be deposited?
choices: Within 5 business days after receipt or lease execution, whichever is later
Within 3 business days after receipt, as with earnest money
Within 24 hours after the firm receives the deposit
Within 3 business days after receipt or lease execution, whichever is earlier
questions.explanation: Property management funds have a 5-business-day deadline, measured from receipt or mutual execution of the lease, whichever is later. The 3-business-day rule applies to other money, such as earnest money.

questions.stem: A brokerage that manages rental properties for owners must keep:
choices: all rents and deposits in one combined trust account
rents and deposits in one trust account, with a separate ledger for each owner
at least one trust account for rents and a separate one for security deposits
security deposits in certificates of deposit for each tenant
questions.explanation: Commission rules require a property management firm to keep rental receipts and security deposits in separate trust or escrow accounts. Trust funds must also stay available without penalty, which rules out CDs absent written agreement.

questions.stem: Which account setup meets Colorado trust account requirements for an LLC brokerage?
choices: A personal savings account in the employing broker's own name at an out-of-state credit union
A money market fund labeled 'broker reserve' and held in the firm's name
An account at an uninsured investment firm, opened in the name of a client
An account in the LLC's name at an FDIC-insured Colorado bank, labeled trust or escrow
questions.explanation: The account must be at a federally insured recognized depository in Colorado, identified as trust or escrow, and held in the firm's name (the entity's name for an LLC).

questions.stem: A broker leaves several months of earned commissions sitting in the firm's trust account "as a cushion." This is:
choices: permitted, as long as the cushion amount stays under $1,000
commingling; money payable to the firm must be withdrawn monthly
conversion, but only once the firm actually spends the money
required, so the firm can cover future bank charges on the account
questions.explanation: Mixing the firm's own money with money belonging to others is commingling, and money payable to the firm must be withdrawn monthly. Firm money may be in the account only in narrow cases, such as funds to cover the account's bank charges or a recorded advance made for a beneficiary; a 'cushion' isn't one of them.

questions.stem: In a monthly three-way reconciliation, which three figures must agree as of the same date?
choices: Journal balance, total of all beneficiary ledgers, and reconciled bank balance
Bank statement balance, the firm's operating account balance, and the MLS sales report
Gross commissions, net commissions, and broker splits
Earnest money receipts, closing statements, and title commitments
questions.explanation: A three-way reconciliation proves that the journal, the total of the ledgers, and the reconciled bank balance all match. Colorado requires it monthly for each trust account holding money belonging to others.

questions.stem: A sale never closed, and the listing contract expired on March 1, 2026. Under Colorado's record retention rule, the broker must keep the transaction file until at least:
choices: March 1, 2027
March 1, 2029
March 1, 2030
March 1, 2031
questions.explanation: Colorado requires records to be kept for four years, measured from closing or, if there is no closing, from the listing contract's expiration date. March 1, 2026 plus four years is March 1, 2030.

questions.stem: The listing brokerage holds earnest money. The deal falls apart and the buyer and seller each demand the money. What should the brokerage do?
choices: Release it to the seller, since the buyer is the one who walked away
Split it equally between the buyer and seller so neither side can sue the firm
Keep it as the firm's commission until the parties settle
Follow the contract, such as continuing to hold it or interpleading it
questions.explanation: The Commission will not discipline a brokerage that holds disputed earnest money as the contract directs. The Commission-approved contract lets the holder keep holding it, interplead it to a court, or follow the contract's notice procedure. A broker may not decide the dispute or keep the money.

questions.stem: A buyer at an open house starts telling a broker about her finances and why she must move quickly. She has signed nothing with the broker. Which statement about the broker's disclosure duty is correct?
choices: Handing her the Definitions of Working Relationships form by itself satisfies the disclosure rule
The broker must give a written brokerage relationship disclosure before discussing this information
No written disclosure is needed until she signs an exclusive right-to-buy contract
A written disclosure is required only if she asks about a relationship the firm doesn't offer
questions.explanation: Commission rules require the written brokerage relationship disclosure before the broker elicits or discusses confidential information such as finances or motivation. The Definitions of Working Relationships form is required only when a party asks about a relationship the firm doesn't offer, and the Division says its definitions section is not, by itself, a disclosure.

questions.stem: A broker is listing a four-unit apartment building that the owner rents to tenants. Which Commission-approved sales contract is the best fit?
choices: Contract to Buy and Sell Real Estate (Residential)
Contract to Buy and Sell Real Estate (Income-Residential)
Contract to Buy and Sell Real Estate (Land)
Contract to Buy and Sell Real Estate (Commercial) with no addendum
questions.explanation: Income-producing residential property, whether 1–4 units or larger, uses the Income-Residential contract. It has provisions for leases, rent rolls, tenant estoppel statements and security deposits that the Residential contract isn't built around.

questions.stem: Under C.R.S. 12-10-403(4), when MUST a Colorado broker use a Commission-approved form?
choices: Only in residential transactions, not commercial or land deals
Only when the buyer is not represented by a Colorado attorney
Whenever one exists and is appropriate for the transaction
Only when the broker is acting as a single agent for a party
questions.explanation: The statute requires a Commission-approved form whenever one exists and is appropriate. Other standard forms, such as attorney-drafted or party-provided forms, are allowed only in the circumstances the law permits.

questions.stem: A buyer asks his broker to write a detailed clause in Additional Provisions that sets out which party bears liability if a neighbor's boundary fence is later found to encroach. What should the broker do?
choices: Draft the clause, since Additional Provisions are not Commission-approved anyway
Copy a similar clause from one of the broker's previous transactions
Refuse to include any language about the fence in the contract
Recommend that an attorney draft it, since drafting it is the practice of law
questions.explanation: Brokers may record simple agreed facts but may not draft legal provisions that allocate rights and liabilities. An attorney should draft that language, and the broker must understand any attorney-drafted clause before using it.

questions.stem: The Conway-Bogue decision allowed Colorado brokers to complete standard forms under certain conditions. Which condition is part of that holding?
choices: No charge for the documents beyond the ordinary commission
The broker must also hold a Colorado law license
The broker may prepare deeds for friends as a favor
The broker may draft custom contracts if both parties consent
questions.explanation: Conway-Bogue (1957) let brokers fill in standard forms only in transactions they are brokering and with no compensation beyond their ordinary commission. Preparing documents as a favor in other transactions or drafting custom contracts is not permitted.

questions.stem: A contract's Dates and Deadlines table sets the Inspection Objection Deadline as "MEC + 5 days." Mutual execution occurred on a Tuesday. On which day does the deadline fall?
choices: Saturday
Monday
Friday
Sunday
questions.explanation: Exclude the first day (Tuesday) and include the last: Wednesday is 1, Thursday 2, Friday 3, Saturday 4, Sunday 5. Whether a Sunday deadline moves to Monday depends on the weekend/holiday Will/Will Not box.

questions.stem: A Colorado residential contract deadline falls on a Sunday. Neither box in the weekend/holiday extension provision is checked, and no Time of Day Deadline applies. When does the deadline expire?
choices: 11:59 p.m. Mountain Time on the following Monday
11:59 p.m. Mountain Time on that Sunday
5:00 p.m. Mountain Time on the preceding Friday
Noon on that Sunday
questions.explanation: If neither box is checked, a deadline that falls on a weekend or holiday is not extended. A day ends at 11:59 p.m. Mountain Time unless a Time of Day Deadline applies to that type of deadline.

questions.stem: The parties enter 5:00 p.m. as the Time of Day Deadline in the Colorado residential contract. Which deadline does that time apply to?
choices: The Closing Date and the time of closing
The Possession Date and Possession Time
The Inspection Objection Deadline
The Acceptance Deadline Date and Time
questions.explanation: The Time of Day Deadline applies to objection, resolution, examination and termination deadlines, such as the Inspection Objection Deadline. Possession and acceptance have their own times in the Dates and Deadlines table, and closing is set by the Closing Date.

questions.stem: A buyer signs the seller's counterproposal at 4:00 p.m. on the acceptance deadline but doesn't tell anyone until the next morning. The counterproposal required acceptance by 6:00 p.m. that day. What is the result?
choices: It expired; the seller never received notice of acceptance in time
A binding contract formed at 4:00 p.m., when the buyer signed
A contract formed because signing came before the 6:00 p.m. deadline
The buyer's original offer revives and binds the seller
questions.explanation: Acceptance requires that the offering party receive notice of acceptance by the deadline. Signing without timely notice doesn't form a contract. The original offer was rejected by the counterproposal and is not revived.

questions.stem: A seller sends a second counterproposal to a buyer before the buyer responds to the first one. What effect does the second counterproposal have?
choices: Both counterproposals are open and the buyer may accept either
It supersedes and replaces the earlier counterproposal
It is invalid without the buyer's consent
It converts the transaction to an Agreement to Amend/Extend
questions.explanation: The Commission's Counterproposal states that it supersedes and replaces any previous counterproposal. Only the latest one can be accepted.

questions.stem: After the contract is fully signed, the lender says it needs an extra week before closing. What should the brokers use to change the Closing Date?
choices: A Counterproposal signed by the seller and sent to the buyer
A new Contract to Buy and Sell replacing the original one
An Agreement to Amend/Extend Contract signed by both parties
A written memo from the listing broker to the closing company
questions.explanation: Changes to a signed contract's dates are made with the Agreement to Amend/Extend Contract, signed by both parties, with notice of acceptance received by its deadline. Brokers can't change deadlines on their own.

questions.stem: A buyer delivers a timely Inspection Objection Notice. The Inspection Resolution Deadline passes with no signed agreement, and the buyer has not withdrawn the objection. What happens?
choices: The contract terminates
Seller must make the repairs
The contract continues as written
Buyer must close, then sue
questions.explanation: Under the Colorado contract, if the parties haven't resolved an inspection objection in writing by the Inspection Resolution Deadline, the contract terminates unless the buyer withdrew the objection in writing before the deadline.

questions.stem: A buyer wants to walk away after an inspection, without negotiating repairs. Which deadline should the buyer use?
choices: Inspection Resolution Deadline
Inspection Termination Deadline
Due Diligence Documents Objection Deadline
New Loan Terms Deadline
questions.explanation: The Inspection Termination Deadline lets the buyer terminate outright over an unsatisfactory condition, as long as the buyer hasn't already delivered an Inspection Objection. The objection and resolution deadlines are for negotiating corrections.

questions.stem: The buyer's appraisal comes in $15,000 below the purchase price on a conventional loan. Which statement is correct under the Colorado residential contract?
choices: The contract terminates automatically at the Appraisal Resolution Deadline
The seller must reduce the price to match the appraised value
The buyer may terminate or object by the Appraisal Objection Deadline
The buyer must close and pay the $15,000 difference in cash
questions.explanation: A low or late appraisal gives the buyer the right to terminate or object by the Appraisal Objection Deadline. Nothing happens automatically. If the buyer doesn't act, the right is lost.

questions.stem: Which loan types have their own appraisal language, so the contract's appraisal deadlines don't apply to them?
choices: Conventional and bond loans
Seller-carry and private loans
Jumbo loans
FHA and VA loans
questions.explanation: The Colorado contract notes that the appraisal deadlines don't apply to FHA-insured or VA-guaranteed loans, which carry their own required appraisal provisions.

questions.stem: A buyer's lender denies the loan, but the buyer doesn't deliver a Notice to Terminate by the New Loan Availability Deadline. The seller is not in default. What is the likely consequence?
choices: The earnest money becomes nonrefundable, except as the contract provides
The contract automatically terminates and all earnest money goes back to the buyer
The seller must extend the deadline
The closing company must refund the earnest money
questions.explanation: If the buyer doesn't timely terminate under the New Loan Availability provision and the seller isn't in default, the earnest money becomes nonrefundable, except as the contract otherwise provides. Time is of the essence.

questions.stem: The Colorado residential contract has no title-company box checked. Who selects the title insurance company and pays for the owner's policy?
choices: The buyer, at the buyer's expense
The seller, at the seller's expense
The listing broker, with costs split equally
The buyer's lender
questions.explanation: If neither box is checked, the seller-selects option applies: the seller selects the title company and pays for the owner's title insurance policy.

questions.stem: A buyer reviews the title commitment and does not object by the Record Title Objection Deadline. What is the effect?
choices: The seller must still remove all exceptions before closing
The buyer may object at closing
The contract terminates
The buyer accepts the condition of title as disclosed
questions.explanation: A buyer who doesn't deliver a timely title objection accepts title as shown. Objections must be received by the deadline because time is of the essence.

questions.stem: Which matter is an off-record title issue the buyer would look for during the Off-Record Title period?
choices: A recorded deed of trust securing the seller's loan
An unrecorded easement shown by a path neighbors use
A recorded subdivision plat showing utility easements
A recorded HOA declaration with use restrictions
questions.explanation: Off-record matters don't appear in the public records. Examples are unrecorded easements, boundary disputes and parties in possession. Recorded documents are reviewed under record title.

questions.stem: A buyer timely objects to an easement shown on the title commitment. The seller doesn't respond, and no written resolution exists by the Title Resolution Deadline. The buyer hasn't withdrawn the objection. What happens?
choices: The contract terminates
Buyer takes title subject to it
Seller is in default and owes damages
Closing is delayed 10 days
questions.explanation: Unresolved title objections work like inspection objections. If there's no written resolution by the Title Resolution Deadline, the contract terminates unless the buyer withdrew the objection first.

questions.stem: Who pays the fee for the owners' association status letter under the Colorado residential contract?
choices: The buyer
The buyer and seller equally
The seller
The listing brokerage firm
questions.explanation: The residential contract makes the seller pay any fee for issuing the association's status letter. Other association fees, such as record-change or working-capital fees, are allocated by checkbox.

questions.stem: A seller asks the listing broker to complete the Seller's Property Disclosure because the broker has seen the house many times. What is the best response?
choices: Complete it, since the broker's observations are more reliable than the seller's
Complete it, then have the seller review and sign it
Leave it blank and let the buyer's inspection cover it
Explain that the seller must complete it from the seller's own knowledge
questions.explanation: The Commission's form is completed by the seller, not the broker, based on the seller's current actual knowledge. The broker separately discloses adverse material facts the broker knows.

questions.stem: Two weeks after delivering the Seller's Property Disclosure, the seller discovers a crack in the foundation. What must happen under the residential contract?
choices: Nothing, because the Seller's Property Disclosure Deadline has passed
The seller may wait and mention it at the closing table
The seller must disclose it, and the buyer gets a short right to terminate
The listing broker decides whether the crack is material enough to disclose
questions.explanation: The seller has a continuing duty to disclose newly discovered adverse material facts. The buyer may then terminate by the earlier of closing or 5 days after receiving the disclosure.

questions.stem: The specific performance box in the buyer-default section is NOT checked, and the buyer defaults. What is the seller's remedy?
choices: The seller may sue for specific performance to force the buyer to close
The seller may keep the earnest money and also sue for actual damages
Seller keeps the earnest money as liquidated damages, its only remedy
The seller must return the earnest money to the buyer and relist
questions.explanation: Unless the specific performance box is checked, liquidated damages apply. The earnest money is the seller's only remedy for buyer default, apart from the buyer's inspection indemnity and the legal-fee provision.

questions.stem: The seller refuses to close on a valid contract, and the buyer is ready to perform. Which remedy is available to the buyer?
choices: Specific performance and/or damages
Only return of the earnest money
Only liquidated damages equal to twice the earnest money
No remedy until mediation is waived by the seller
questions.explanation: If the seller defaults, the buyer may cancel, recover the earnest money and seek damages, or seek specific performance and/or damages. Mediation must be attempted first but doesn't eliminate these remedies.

questions.stem: A dispute arises over who gets the earnest money after a failed transaction. What must the parties do before filing a lawsuit or arbitration, under the residential contract?
choices: Nothing; either party may sue or demand arbitration immediately
Submit the dispute to binding arbitration administered by the title company
Ask the Real Estate Commission to hold a hearing and decide it
Attempt mediation, which ends if unresolved 30 days after the request
questions.explanation: The contract requires good-faith mediation before arbitration or litigation. Costs are split equally, and the duty to mediate ends if the dispute isn't resolved within 30 days of the written mediation request.

questions.stem: The buyer properly terminated and the seller has received an Earnest Money Release. How long does the seller have to sign it before being in default?
choices: 3 days after receipt
10 days after receipt
30 days after receipt
120 days after receipt
questions.explanation: When the buyer is entitled to the earnest money, the contract requires the seller to sign the release instructions within three days of receiving them (and the buyer has the same duty when the seller is entitled). Not signing on time is a default.

questions.stem: Buyer and seller each claim the earnest money and won't sign a release. The Earnest Money Holder sends a notice under the contract's dispute provision. If no court case number is received in time, the holder may return the money to the buyer. How long is that period?
choices: 30 days
60 days
120 days
180 days
questions.explanation: Under the earnest money dispute provision, the holder may return the earnest money to the buyer unless it receives a case number within 120 days of its notice to the parties. The holder may also wait or interplead the funds.

questions.stem: A buyer's Notice to Terminate arrives one day after the applicable termination deadline. What is the effect?
choices: It is effective because it was mailed before the deadline
It is ineffective, and that termination right is waived
It is effective if the seller has not yet closed
It extends the deadline automatically
questions.explanation: Termination is effective on the other party's receipt of a written notice by the deadline. A late notice is ineffective and the right is waived, because time is of the essence.

questions.stem: Under the Colorado residential contract, delivery of a notice to which person counts as delivery to the seller before closing?
choices: Only the seller personally, at the seller's address
The title company handling the closing
The buyer's lender or mortgage broker
The seller's broker or brokerage firm
questions.explanation: Before closing, a notice is effective when received by the party or by the broker or brokerage firm working with that party. Notices after closing (and electronic notices after cancellation or termination) must be received by the party itself.

questions.stem: No deed type is selected in the residential contract. What deed must the seller deliver at closing?
choices: General warranty deed
Quitclaim deed
Special warranty deed
Bargain and sale deed
questions.explanation: If no other deed is selected, the seller must deliver a good and sufficient special warranty deed.

questions.stem: A listing expired. Ten days later, the seller sells directly to a buyer the listing broker had negotiated with and named to the seller in writing during the listing. The listing has a 60-day holdover period, and the seller has not signed a listing with any other firm. Is compensation owed?
choices: No, because compensation is earned only during the listing period
Yes, because the buyer is a Submitted Prospect and the sale is in holdover
Only if the buyer had also signed an exclusive right-to-buy contract
No, because the seller, not the broker, negotiated the final sale after expiration
questions.explanation: The holdover clause covers a sale during the holdover period to a person the broker negotiated with and named to the seller in writing during the listing period. The Will/Will Not box only matters when another firm earns a commission under a new exclusive listing signed during the holdover, which didn't happen here.

questions.stem: In the Exclusive Right-to-Sell Listing Contract, neither box is checked on whether the seller consents to disclosing the existence of offers. A buyer's broker asks whether there are other offers. What may the listing broker do?
choices: Disclose how many offers there are, but not their prices or terms
Disclose the terms if the buyer's broker promises to keep them confidential
Disclose everything, since multiple offers are public information
Decline to disclose that offers exist, since the seller hasn't consented
questions.explanation: If neither box is checked, the seller does not consent to disclosing that offers exist. Disclosing the terms of any offer always requires the seller's written consent.

questions.stem: A property is under contract, and the listing broker receives another written offer. What must the seller's agent do?
choices: Present it to the seller in a timely manner
Hold it until the first contract fails
Return it, because the property is under contract
Present it only if it is higher than the existing contract price
questions.explanation: Colorado law and the listing contract require a seller's agent to present all offers in a timely manner, even when the property is under contract. A seller who accepts should make it a backup contract.

questions.stem: Which Commission-approved document is completed by the listing licensee and states the measurement source and that square footage is for marketing purposes only?
choices: Seller's Property Disclosure
Square Footage Disclosure
Source of Water Addendum
Closing Instructions
questions.explanation: The Square Footage Disclosure is completed by the listing licensee. It identifies whether the licensee measured, the standard used, and other sources, and it warns the buyer to measure independently if exact size matters.

questions.stem: A homeowner in foreclosure who lives in the home agrees to sell it to an investor who will not live there. No short sale is involved. Which contract is required?
choices: The standard Residential contract with a Short Sale Addendum attached
The Land contract with a Residential Addendum
The Residential (Colorado Foreclosure Protection Act) contract
An attorney-drafted contract only
questions.explanation: When the seller occupies the home as a principal residence, the buyer won't occupy it, and the buyer knows the seller is in default or at least 30 days delinquent (as in foreclosure), the Colorado Foreclosure Protection Act version of the residential contract applies. It comes with a Seller Warning and Notice of Cancellation. A short sale would instead use the standard contract with a Short Sale Addendum.

questions.stem: Under the Colorado Foreclosure Protection Act, how long does a homeowner who signs a contract with an equity purchaser have to cancel?
choices: Midnight of the 3rd business day after signing or noon the day before the sale, whichever is earlier
Until 10 calendar days after signing, or until closing if that comes first
Midnight of the 5th business day after signing or the day of the sale, whichever is later
Until 30 days after the foreclosure sale, during the redemption period
questions.explanation: C.R.S. 6-1-1113 lets the homeowner cancel until the earlier of midnight of the third business day after signing or noon on the day before the foreclosure sale.

questions.stem: A seller will carry back a note from the buyer. What may the broker who is handling the sale do?
choices: Draft custom default and acceleration terms if the seller has no attorney
Fill in the Commission-approved note and deed of trust forms, with no extra fee
Charge a separate document-preparation fee for the note and the deed of trust
Act as the lender of record so the seller financing is properly documented
questions.explanation: Under the forms statute and Conway-Bogue, a broker may complete Commission-approved notes and deeds of trust in a transaction the broker is handling, with no charge beyond the commission. Custom drafting requires an attorney. The forms warn the parties to consult counsel in a consumer credit transaction, and the residential contract warns that, unless exempt, financing documents should be prepared by an attorney or licensed mortgage loan originator.

questions.stem: Who signs the Commission-approved Closing Instructions?
choices: Buyer, seller and the closing company
The listing broker and the buyer's broker
Only the buyer's lender and the closing company
Buyer and seller only
questions.explanation: Buyer, seller and the closing company sign the Closing Instructions, which engage the closing company for closing and settlement services. Changing them requires a writing signed by all three.

questions.stem: A title company is closing a sale in which Broker Ana represents the buyer. The title company prepares the closing statement. Under Colorado Commission rules, who is responsible for making sure the buyer receives an accurate, complete closing statement?
choices: Only the title company, because it prepared the statement
Ana, the broker with the brokerage relationship
The buyer's lender
No one, because the buyer signs to approve the statement
questions.explanation: Commission rules make the broker who has a brokerage relationship responsible for the proper closing and for ensuring the consumer receives an accurate, complete, detailed closing statement signed by the broker. Using a title company delegates the work, not the responsibility.

questions.stem: A broker cannot attend a closing because of a family emergency. What does Colorado's closing rule allow?
choices: A firm-designated broker may review and attend in her place, sharing responsibility
The broker may let the title company close alone, with no further broker involvement
The closing must be postponed until the broker can attend and sign the statement in person
The broker's unlicensed assistant may attend the closing and sign the closing statement
questions.explanation: The broker must attend or be reasonably available; a firm-designated substitute broker may attend instead and then assumes joint responsibility for the statement's accuracy, completeness and delivery.

questions.stem: Who signs the Commission-approved Closing Instructions form?
choices: The listing broker and the buyer's broker
Only the closing company
The buyer's lender, the seller and the closing company
The buyer, the seller and the closing company
questions.explanation: Closing Instructions engage the closing company for the parties, so the buyer, seller and closing company sign. Brokers are not parties to the instructions.

questions.stem: Under Colorado's good funds law, which payment may a closing company generally disburse against immediately?
choices: A buyer's personal check for the down payment
A post-dated check from the seller
A wire transfer that has been received
A promise from the lender to wire funds tomorrow
questions.explanation: Disbursement may occur only after funds are received and available for immediate withdrawal; wires and cashier's, certified or teller's checks qualify. Personal checks and promised funds do not.

questions.stem: A home sells for $512,000. What is the Colorado documentary fee?
questions.explanation: The fee is one cent per $100 of consideration: $512,000 / 100 = 5,120 x $0.01 = $51.20.

questions.stem: Under the Colorado Contract to Buy and Sell Real Estate (Residential), if neither title box is checked, who selects the title company and pays for the owner's title insurance policy?
choices: The seller
The buyer
The buyer and seller split it equally
The buyer's lender
questions.explanation: The contract defaults to the seller-selects option, under which the seller selects the title company and pays for the owner's policy. Many other states use buyer-paid owner's policies, which makes this a common trap.

questions.stem: Colorado property taxes for 2026 become due on which date?
choices: January 1, 2026
April 30, 2026
January 1, 2027
questions.explanation: Colorado taxes are due January 1 of the year after they are levied, so they are paid in arrears. That's why the seller is usually debited for the current-year taxes at closing.

questions.stem: Closing is in July. Current-year property taxes have not been paid. How are the seller's share of the taxes shown on the closing statement?
choices: Credit seller, debit buyer
Debit buyer only
Debit seller, credit buyer
Credit seller only
questions.explanation: Because taxes are paid in arrears, the buyer will pay the whole year's bill later. The seller owes the buyer for the seller's days of ownership, so it is a seller debit and a buyer credit.

questions.stem: Last year's taxes were $3,650. Closing is June 15 in a 365-day year; the buyer owns the day of closing and current taxes are unpaid. Using the Colorado contract's default basis, what is the tax proration?
choices: Credit seller and debit buyer $1,650
Debit seller and credit buyer $1,650
Debit seller and credit buyer $2,000
Debit seller and credit buyer $1,825
questions.explanation: Daily rate $3,650 / 365 = $10. Seller's days are January 1 through June 14 = 165 days, so 165 x $10 = $1,650, debited to the seller and credited to the buyer because taxes are paid in arrears.

questions.stem: Unless the parties agree otherwise, the Colorado residential contract prorates general real estate taxes based on:
choices: The prior calendar year's taxes, using the latest mill levy and valuation
An estimate of the current year's taxes supplied by the listing broker
The average of the last three years of taxes shown by the county treasurer
The current year's taxes, re-prorated once the actual tax bill is issued
questions.explanation: The default basis is the taxes for the calendar year immediately before closing, using the most recent mill levy and assessed valuation. Prorations are final unless the parties agree otherwise in writing.

questions.stem: A seller collected June rent of $1,800 on June 1. Closing is June 15 (30-day month) and the buyer owns the day of closing. What is the rent proration?
choices: Credit seller and debit buyer $960
Debit seller and credit buyer $840
Credit seller and debit buyer $840
Debit seller and credit buyer $960
questions.explanation: Daily rent is $1,800 / 30 = $60. The buyer owns June 15 through June 30, 16 days: 16 x $60 = $960. The seller collected rent belonging to the buyer, so the seller is debited.

questions.stem: How are tenants' security deposits typically handled on the closing statement when a rental property is sold with leases assigned to the buyer?
choices: Prorated between buyer and seller by the days left on each lease
Credit seller and debit buyer the full amount of the deposits
Debit seller and credit buyer the full amount of the deposits
Left off the statement and refunded directly to the tenants
questions.explanation: Security deposits belong to the tenants and are transferred in full, not prorated: the seller is debited and the buyer credited. The contract also requires the seller to notify tenants in writing.

questions.stem: The seller prepaid $300 in HOA dues for June. Closing is June 15 (30-day month); the buyer owns the day of closing. How is this shown?
choices: Debit seller and credit buyer $160
Credit seller and debit buyer $160
Credit seller and debit buyer $140
Debit seller and credit buyer $140
questions.explanation: The daily amount is $10, and the buyer gets 16 days (June 15 to 30), so $160. The seller paid in advance for days the buyer will enjoy, so the seller is credited and the buyer debited.

questions.stem: On a closing statement, the buyer's earnest money deposit is shown as:
choices: A credit to the buyer
A debit to the buyer
A credit to the seller
A debit to the seller
questions.explanation: Earnest money has already been paid toward the price, so the buyer is credited. It is not a separate seller entry because the seller is credited with the full purchase price.

questions.stem: Which item would appear ONLY on the seller's side of a closing statement?
choices: Purchase price
Property tax proration
Proration of HOA dues the seller prepaid
Payoff of the seller's existing loan
questions.explanation: Loan payoffs go to a third party (the seller's lender), so they appear only as a seller debit. The price and prorations are between buyer and seller, so they appear on both sides.

questions.stem: A seller who lives in Arizona sells a $350,000 Colorado rental property. Absent an exemption, what must the closing company do under Colorado law?
choices: Withhold 15% of the amount realized and remit it to the IRS under FIRPTA
Withhold nothing, because the seller is a U.S. citizen and not a foreign person
Withhold the lesser of 2% of the price or net proceeds for the Colorado Department of Revenue
Collect a 2% state transfer tax from the buyer and pay it to the county clerk and recorder
questions.explanation: Colorado requires the closing company to withhold the lesser of 2% of the price or net proceeds from nonresident sellers when the price exceeds $100,000, unless an exemption applies. FIRPTA (federal) applies to foreign persons, not to U.S. residents of other states.

questions.stem: Under Colorado law, the maximum security deposit a residential landlord may require is:
choices: One month's rent
Two months' rent
Three months' rent
There is no maximum
questions.explanation: A 2023 statute (C.R.S. 38-12-102.5) caps residential security deposits at two months' rent.

questions.stem: A residential lease is silent about the deposit return period. The tenant moves out and the landlord accepts the premises on March 31. By when must the landlord return the deposit or provide a written statement of deductions?
choices: Within 30 days
Within 10 business days
Within 60 days
Within 90 days
questions.explanation: Since January 1, 2026, Colorado gives the landlord 30 days after the lease ends or the premises are surrendered, whichever is later; a lease can extend that to no more than 60 days. Since this lease is silent, 30 days applies.

questions.stem: A landlord willfully keeps a tenant's deposit without cause. Under Colorado law, the landlord can be liable for:
choices: Only the amount withheld, with each side paying its own attorney fees
Twice the amount withheld, plus court costs but not attorney fees
A fixed $500 statutory penalty in addition to the deposit itself
Treble the amount wrongfully withheld, plus attorney fees and costs
questions.explanation: Wrongful retention exposes the landlord to treble the amount wrongfully withheld plus reasonable attorney fees and court costs, after the tenant gives at least 7 days' notice before suing.

questions.stem: A tenant falls behind on rent in a typical Colorado apartment. Before filing an eviction for nonpayment, the landlord generally must give a written demand allowing the tenant how long to pay or move?
choices: 3 days
30 days
10 days
24 hours
questions.explanation: C.R.S. 13-40-104 generally requires 10 days' written notice for residential nonpayment. Shorter periods apply only to exempt small-landlord agreements (5 days) and nonresidential or employer-provided housing (3 days).

questions.stem: Which of the following is a protected class under the Colorado Fair Housing Act but NOT under the federal Fair Housing Act?
choices: Familial status
Marital status
Disability
National origin
questions.explanation: Colorado adds marital status, creed, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, ancestry, veteran or military status, and source of income. Familial status, disability and national origin are protected by both.

questions.stem: A Colorado landlord refuses to rent to an applicant because her rent would be paid partly with a housing voucher. This most likely violates Colorado law based on:
choices: Source of income
Familial status
Creed
Gender expression
questions.explanation: Colorado protects lawful, verifiable sources of income, including rental assistance, though some small landlords are exempt from parts of these provisions.

questions.stem: Colorado water law is based on which doctrine?
choices: Riparian rights (reasonable use by streamside owners)
Littoral rights
Correlative rights based on acreage
Prior appropriation (first in time, first in right)
questions.explanation: Colorado uses prior appropriation: the earliest beneficial user holds the senior right. Owning land along a stream does not by itself give a right to use the water.

questions.stem: A buyer is purchasing a home with a domestic exempt well used for household purposes. Under Colorado law, how is the well's change of ownership handled?
choices: The seller files a well transfer notice with the county assessor before the home is listed
The listing broker files the change form with the water court at the closing table
The buyer completes the form; the closing company files it with the state within 60 days
No filing is needed, because exempt wells are outside the State Engineer's permit system
questions.explanation: The buyer completes the Division of Water Resources change in owner name form; the closing service provider submits it to the Division within 60 days after closing (or the buyer files it if there is no closing company).

questions.stem: A county assessor values a home at $400,000. If the assessment rate is 6.5% and the total mill levy is 90 mills, what is the annual property tax?
In a Colorado public trustee foreclosure, by when must the homeowner file a notice of intent to cure?
choices: At least 15 calendar days before the sale
Within 8 business days after the sale
At any time up to the moment of the sale
By noon on the day of the foreclosure sale
questions.explanation: The owner must file a notice of intent to cure no later than 15 calendar days before the sale and pay the cure amount by noon the day before the sale. Colorado owners have no post-sale redemption right.

questions.stem: An investor wants to buy the principal residence of an owner who is 60 days behind on the mortgage. It is not a short sale. Under the Colorado Foreclosure Protection Act, how long does the homeowner have to cancel the contract with this equity purchaser?
choices: Until the closing date, as long as the investor has not yet recorded the deed
For five calendar days after signing, by written notice delivered to the investor
There is no right to cancel once the homeowner has signed a compliant contract
Until midnight of the 3rd business day after signing, or noon the day before the sale if earlier
questions.explanation: C.R.S. 6-1-1113 lets the homeowner cancel an equity purchase contract until midnight of the third business day after signing, or noon on the day before the foreclosure sale, whichever comes first.

questions.stem: A seller bought her home for $300,000 and later added a $40,000 kitchen remodel. She sells for $450,000 and pays $25,000 in selling costs. What is her gain?
A married couple filing jointly sells the main home they have owned and lived in together for six years. Their gain is $620,000. How much of the gain is taxable?
questions.explanation: They meet the 2-out-of-5-year ownership and use tests, so they can exclude up to $500,000 on a joint return. $620,000 − $500,000 = $120,000 is taxable.

questions.stem: An investor buys a rental house for $440,000. The land is valued at $110,000. Using straight-line cost recovery over 27.5 years, what is the annual depreciation deduction?
questions.explanation: Land isn't depreciable, so the depreciable basis is $440,000 − $110,000 = $330,000. $330,000 ÷ 27.5 = $12,000. Dividing the full $440,000 by 27.5 gives $16,000, which wrongly includes the land.

questions.stem: An investor bought a rental property for $275,000 and has taken $8,000 per year in depreciation for 5 years. No improvements were made. What is the investor's adjusted basis?
questions.explanation: Depreciation reduces basis. Total depreciation is $8,000 × 5 = $40,000, so adjusted basis is $275,000 − $40,000 = $235,000.

questions.stem: Which single seller qualifies for the full $250,000 home-sale exclusion?
choices: A seller who owned the home 4 years but lived in it only the first 18 months before renting it out
A seller who owned and lived in the home for 5 years but used the exclusion on another home 10 months ago
A seller who has owned and lived in the home for 30 months
A seller who owned a vacation cabin for 10 years and visited it every summer
questions.explanation: The seller must own and use the home as a main home for at least 2 years (24 months) of the 5 years before the sale, and generally can't have used the exclusion within the past 2 years. Thirty months of ownership and use meets both tests; 18 months of use does not.

questions.stem: An investor sells a lot for a profit. For the gain to be treated as a long-term capital gain, how long must the investor have held the lot?
choices: More than one year
At least six months
At least two years
More than five years
questions.explanation: Assets held more than one year produce long-term capital gain, which gets preferential rates. Gains on assets held one year or less are short-term and taxed like ordinary income.

questions.stem: Which exchange could qualify as a Section 1031 like-kind exchange?
choices: Trading a primary residence for a rental duplex
A developer trading newly built homes held for sale for an apartment building
Trading a vacation cabin used only by the family for raw land
Trading an investment apartment building for investment land
questions.explanation: Like-kind treatment applies to real property held for investment or business use, and different kinds of real estate (an apartment building and raw land) are like-kind to each other. A primary residence, a personal vacation home, and property held for sale don't qualify.

questions.stem: An investor closes the sale of a warehouse as the first half of a 1031 exchange. Within how many days must the investor identify replacement property in writing?
choices: 30 days
45 days
90 days
180 days
questions.explanation: The investor has 45 days to identify replacement property and 180 days (or the tax return due date, including extensions, if earlier) to acquire it. Both periods start when the old property is transferred.

questions.stem: In a 1031 exchange, an investor receives a replacement property plus $40,000 in cash. The investor's realized gain is $150,000. How is the cash treated?
choices: The $40,000 is taxable gain in the year of the exchange
The entire $150,000 becomes taxable
The cash is tax-free because the exchange qualifies
The cash reduces the basis of the replacement property but is never taxed
questions.explanation: Cash received is boot. Gain is recognized up to the amount of boot, so $40,000 is taxable now; the remaining $110,000 is deferred. Receiving boot doesn't disqualify the whole exchange.

questions.stem: An investor client asks his listing broker to hold the sale proceeds of his rental property in the brokerage trust account until he buys a replacement property in a 1031 exchange. What should the broker do?
choices: Agree, because funds held in a trust account are not considered received by the seller
Agree, as long as the funds are released within 180 days
Explain that a qualified intermediary should hold the proceeds and recommend he consult a tax professional
Have the closing company wire the funds to the investor so he can purchase the replacement property directly
questions.explanation: The client's own agent generally can't serve as the qualified intermediary, and if the investor takes control of the cash the exchange can fail. The broker should point the client to a qualified intermediary and a tax professional rather than structure the exchange.

questions.stem: A seller finances the sale of a lot and will receive principal payments over the next 10 years. How is the seller's gain generally reported for federal income tax purposes?
choices: All in the year of sale, no matter when the payments arrive
Proportionally as principal payments are received
Only after the final payment is received
Never, because seller-financed gain is tax-exempt
questions.explanation: In an installment sale the seller receives at least one payment after the year of sale and generally reports the gain proportionally as principal is collected. Interest received is taxed separately as ordinary income.

questions.stem: How are funds from a construction loan typically disbursed?
choices: In one lump sum to the builder at loan closing
To the borrower in equal monthly amounts regardless of progress
In draws as stages of construction are completed and inspected
Only after a certificate of occupancy is issued
questions.explanation: Construction lenders release funds in draws tied to completed, inspected work. This keeps the loan balance in line with the value actually added to the property.

questions.stem: A developer obtains a short-term loan to build an office building. When the building is finished, a life insurance company will make a long-term loan that pays off the construction lender. What is the long-term loan called?
choices: A bridge loan
A blanket loan
A wraparound loan
A takeout loan
questions.explanation: A takeout (permanent) loan replaces the interim construction loan once construction is complete. A bridge loan covers a gap between buying and selling, which is a different situation.

questions.stem: A buyer wants to build a custom home and prefers to close only once, with financing that automatically converts to a regular mortgage when the home is complete. What type of loan fits?
choices: Construction-to-permanent loan
Takeout commitment only
Home equity line of credit
Blanket loan with partial release clauses
questions.explanation: A construction-to-permanent loan funds construction and then converts to long-term financing, usually with a single closing. A separate construction loan plus a takeout loan requires two loans, and a blanket loan covers several parcels.

questions.stem: Before releasing each construction draw, a lender asks for lien waivers from the contractor and suppliers and updates the title search. What is the main reason?
choices: To verify the borrower's income before each payment is released
To protect the lender's lien position against mechanic's liens
To update the property's assessed value for tax purposes
To set the interest rate for the permanent loan
questions.explanation: Unpaid contractors and suppliers can file mechanic's liens, which can threaten the lender's position. Lien waivers and title updates confirm the money paid out so far actually reached the people doing the work.

questions.stem: Which body writes and interprets the Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice (USPAP)?
choices: The Association of Real Estate License Law Officials (ARELLO)
The Appraisal Standards Board of The Appraisal Foundation
The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau
Each state's real estate commission
questions.explanation: The Appraisal Standards Board, part of The Appraisal Foundation, develops and interprets USPAP. ARELLO is an association of real estate license regulators and has no role in appraisal standards.

questions.stem: A buyer's broker is worried a home won't appraise at the contract price. Which action is permitted?
choices: Calling the appraiser to say the deal falls apart below the contract price
Asking the lender to order a new appraiser who will 'hit the number'
Telling the appraiser future referrals depend on a supportive value
Asking, through the lender, that the appraiser consider recent sales
questions.explanation: Appraisal independence rules allow asking the appraiser to consider additional relevant information, such as comparable sales. Pressuring for a target value, shopping for an appraiser to hit a number, or tying future work to the result is prohibited.

questions.stem: A lender needs an appraisal of a regional shopping center. Which appraiser credential level is qualified to appraise this property?
choices: Certified general
Certified residential
Licensed residential
Trainee
questions.explanation: Only a certified general appraiser may appraise all types of real property, including commercial property. Residential credentials are limited to 1–4 unit residential property, and a trainee works only under a certified appraiser's supervision.

questions.stem: A retail tenant pays $2,500 per month base rent plus 5% of annual gross sales above the natural breakpoint. Annual gross sales are $800,000. What is the tenant's total annual rent?
questions.explanation: Annual base rent is $30,000, so the natural breakpoint is $30,000 ÷ 0.05 = $600,000. Overage is $200,000 × 5% = $10,000, for total rent of $40,000. $10,000 is only the percentage rent.

questions.stem: A percentage lease calls for annual base rent of $48,000 and 8% of gross sales above the natural breakpoint. What is the natural breakpoint?
questions.explanation: Natural breakpoint = annual base rent ÷ percentage rate = $48,000 ÷ 0.08 = $600,000. At that sales level, 8% of sales equals the base rent.

questions.stem: A tenant leases 3,000 sq ft in a 24,000 sq ft building on a triple net lease at $18 per sq ft per year. The building's annual taxes, insurance and maintenance total $120,000 and are shared pro rata. What is the tenant's total monthly payment?
questions.explanation: Base rent is 3,000 × $18 = $54,000 a year. The tenant's share is 12.5% of $120,000 = $15,000. Total $69,000 ÷ 12 = $5,750 a month. $4,500 is base rent only.

questions.stem: Under which lease does the tenant pay base rent plus the property taxes, insurance and maintenance, giving the landlord the most predictable income?
choices: Gross lease
Graduated (step-up) lease
Percentage lease
Triple net lease
questions.explanation: In a triple net (NNN) lease the tenant pays rent plus taxes, insurance and maintenance. In a gross lease the landlord pays those costs out of a fixed rent.

questions.stem: A developer leases vacant land for 75 years and constructs an office building on it. This arrangement is a:
choices: Ground lease
Graduated lease
Index lease
Gross lease
questions.explanation: A ground lease rents only the land, usually for a long term, and the tenant builds improvements. The long term lets the tenant finance and recover the building's cost.

questions.stem: A shopping center tenant pays a monthly charge for its share of parking lot repairs, landscaping and snow removal. This charge is best described as:
choices: A tenant improvement allowance
Common area maintenance
Percentage rent
Delay rental
questions.explanation: Common area maintenance (CAM) charges cover the upkeep of shared areas, usually allocated pro rata and reconciled annually.

questions.stem: A prospective office tenant and a landlord sign a letter of intent outlining rent, term and a tenant improvement allowance. Unless it states otherwise, the letter of intent typically:
choices: Is a binding lease for the term and rent stated in it
Transfers possession of the space to the tenant at signing
Is a non-binding summary of the proposed terms
Must be recorded in the county records to be effective
questions.explanation: An LOI usually sets out key terms for negotiating the full lease and is written to be non-binding on the deal itself, though specific clauses such as confidentiality may be binding.

questions.stem: In a commercial lease transaction, the split of the commission between the landlord's broker and the tenant's broker is determined by:
choices: State law
The local Realtor association's fee schedule
The MLS's standard commission rate
Agreement among the parties and brokers
questions.explanation: Commission amounts and splits are set by agreement. No law or association sets them, and brokers agreeing on rates among themselves would be price fixing.

questions.stem: A broker is selling a dry-cleaning business, including its equipment, customer list, inventory and good name. The value of the business's reputation and customer loyalty is called:
choices: Goodwill
Inventory
Fixtures
Chattel mortgage
questions.explanation: Goodwill is the intangible value of a business's reputation and customer relationships. It is part of a business opportunity sale but is not real property.

questions.stem: Under an oil and gas lease, a landowner receives a one-time payment when the lease is signed, regardless of whether any oil is found. This payment is the:
choices: Royalty
Bonus
Delay rental
Shut-in payment
questions.explanation: The bonus is paid at signing and kept whether or not production occurs. A royalty is a share of actual production, and a delay rental keeps the lease alive without drilling during the primary term.

questions.stem: An oil and gas lease has a five-year primary term. In year three a well begins producing in paying quantities and continues producing for 20 years. The lease:
choices: Ends at the end of the five-year primary term
Converts to a periodic tenancy
Continues as long as production continues
Requires the lessee to pay delay rentals for 20 years
questions.explanation: Once production in paying quantities begins, the lease is held by production and continues beyond the primary term for as long as production lasts.

questions.stem: Which statement about a multiple listing service is correct?
choices: It is a state agency that licenses brokers
Membership rules are set by federal law and are identical nationwide
Placing a listing in the MLS makes every member broker an agent of the seller
It is a private organization through which members share listing information
questions.explanation: An MLS is a private cooperative arrangement among brokers, and its membership rules vary. Cooperating through the MLS does not by itself create agency with the seller.

questions.stem: A broker displays other brokerages' active listings on her website through IDX. Under typical MLS IDX rules, she must:
choices: Identify the listing brokerage on each listing display
Rewrite each listing's remarks and photos in her own words
Show the seller's name and phone number on every listing
Remove the MLS as the source to avoid confusing consumers
questions.explanation: IDX rules generally require the listing firm to be identified in a reasonably prominent location and the MLS credited as the source. Displaying brokers may not alter another firm's listing content.

questions.stem: A seller tells her listing broker she does not want her home shown on any websites. What should the broker do?
choices: Refuse, because IDX display is mandatory once a listing is entered in the MLS
Honor it and have the MLS withhold the listing from internet display
Cancel the listing agreement, since internet exposure is required
Display the listing only on the broker's own website instead
questions.explanation: Typical MLS rules let a seller direct the listing broker to withhold the listing, or just the address, from internet display. The broker follows the seller's instruction and the MLS's procedure.

questions.stem: A property manager buys social media ads for a new apartment complex and chooses to show them only to users aged 25 to 40 with no children. This is a concern because:
choices: Social media housing ads must be reviewed and approved by HUD before they run
Only print advertising, not online advertising, is covered by the Fair Housing Act's ad rules
Targeting that excludes families with children can violate the Fair Housing Act
Age is the only characteristic that matters in apartment advertising
questions.explanation: The Fair Housing Act's advertising rules apply online, and selecting audiences so that a protected group (here, familial status) doesn't learn about housing can be discriminatory even if the ad's wording is neutral.

questions.stem: Under the federal E-SIGN Act, which document still requires traditional (non-electronic) treatment?
choices: A purchase contract signed by both parties
A listing agreement
A residential lease application
A will
questions.explanation: E-SIGN excludes wills, codicils and testamentary trusts, along with family-law matters, court documents and certain notices. Ordinary real estate contracts can be signed electronically.

questions.stem: Before a business may deliver legally required consumer disclosures electronically under the E-SIGN Act, the consumer must:
choices: Affirmatively consent after being told of the right to receive paper copies
Sign a paper waiver of the right to paper copies in front of a notary
Agree in writing to pay a fee for receiving disclosures electronically
Live in a state that has not adopted the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act
questions.explanation: E-SIGN requires the consumer's affirmative consent after disclosures about paper copies, withdrawing consent and system requirements, given in a way that shows the consumer can access the records.

questions.stem: Two days before closing, a buyer receives an email that appears to come from the title company with new wiring instructions. The buyer's broker should advise the buyer to:
choices: Wire the funds right away so the closing isn't delayed by the change
Call the title company at an independently obtained number to verify
Reply to the email asking the sender to confirm the new account number
Call the phone number in the email's signature block to confirm the change
questions.explanation: Changed wiring instructions by email are a classic wire fraud sign. Verification should be by phone to a known, independently obtained number; contact details in the suspicious email may belong to the criminal.

questions.stem: A broker's office policy for safety requires agents to meet new prospects at the office and copy their photo ID before a showing. To avoid a fair housing problem, the policy should be:
choices: Applied only to prospects who seem suspicious
Used only for buyers from outside the area
Applied consistently to every new prospect
Waived for prospects who prefer not to show ID
questions.explanation: Safety policies are fine, but applying them selectively based on how someone looks or sounds can be discriminatory. Apply the same rule to everyone.

questions.stem: Which practice best protects clients' personal information held by a brokerage?
choices: Keeping copies of every document indefinitely in case they are ever needed
Emailing bank statements to clients and lenders as regular attachments
Sharing one MLS and email login among the whole team for convenience
Keeping only needed information and securely disposing of the rest
questions.explanation: The FTC's guidance for businesses stresses keeping only what you need, protecting it, and disposing of it properly. Shared logins and unencrypted email increase risk.

questions.stem: On a six-column Colorado settlement worksheet, how is the payoff of the seller's existing mortgage entered?
choices: Seller debit and buyer credit, no cash entry
Seller debit and broker (cash) credit
Buyer debit and seller credit
Seller credit and broker (cash) debit
questions.explanation: The payoff reduces the seller's proceeds (seller debit) and is a check the closing pays out to the seller's lender (broker credit). It is not a buyer entry, because the buyer isn't taking over that loan.

questions.stem: A buyer is financing the purchase with a new $320,000 loan from a bank. How does the loan appear on the settlement worksheet?
choices: Buyer credit and seller debit
Seller credit and broker (cash) debit, no buyer entry
Buyer debit and broker (cash) credit
Buyer credit and broker (cash) debit
questions.explanation: Loan funds come from the lender, an outsider, so it's a single entry: a credit to the buyer and a receipt (debit) in the cash column. The seller is paid the full price, so the new loan never touches the seller's side.

questions.stem: A buyer assumes the seller's existing loan with a $185,000 balance. How is the assumed balance entered?
choices: Seller debit and buyer credit only
Buyer credit and broker (cash) debit
Seller debit and broker (cash) credit
Buyer debit and seller credit
questions.explanation: With an assumption no money changes hands: the seller accepts the buyer's takeover of the debt as part of the price. It's a double entry — debit seller, credit buyer — and nothing goes through the cash column.

questions.stem: The seller agrees to carry back a $40,000 promissory note secured by a second deed of trust. On the worksheet this note is:
choices: A credit to the seller and a debit to the buyer
A credit to the buyer and a cash receipt
A debit to the seller and a credit to the buyer
A debit to the seller and a cash disbursement at closing
questions.explanation: The seller takes a note instead of $40,000 of cash, which reduces the seller's cash proceeds; the buyer pays $40,000 less in cash. No money moves at closing, so there's no cash-column entry.

questions.stem: How is the buyer's $12,000 earnest money deposit, held by the closing company, entered on a six-column worksheet?
choices: Buyer credit and seller debit, no cash entry
Seller credit and buyer debit
Buyer credit and broker (cash) debit
Buyer debit and broker (cash) credit
questions.explanation: The deposit is money the buyer has already paid toward the price, so the buyer is credited. It's money the closing has received, so it's a cash debit (receipt). The seller is already credited with the full price, so earnest money is never a seller entry.

questions.stem: Which of these items is a double entry (one party debited, the other credited)?
choices: The seller's share of unpaid current-year taxes
The seller's brokerage fee under the listing contract
The lender's title policy the buyer pays for
The buyer's new first mortgage from a bank
questions.explanation: Prorated taxes move value between the parties: the seller is debited for the days the seller owned the property and the buyer is credited because the buyer will pay the whole bill. The other items involve only one party and an outsider.

questions.stem: Which item normally appears on only one party's side of the worksheet?
choices: The purchase price agreed in the contract
Tenant security deposits transferred to the buyer
Rent the seller collected for days after closing
The brokerage fee the seller pays
questions.explanation: The brokerage fee is between the seller and the brokerage firm, so it's a seller debit (and a cash disbursement) only. The price, deposits and rent prorations are all double entries between buyer and seller.

questions.stem: A Colorado home sells for $436,700, and the parties agreed that the buyer will pay the state documentary fee. How is the fee entered on the worksheet?
choices: $43.67 seller debit and cash credit
$43.67 buyer debit and cash credit
$436.70 buyer debit and cash credit
$43.67 buyer debit and seller credit
questions.explanation: The documentary fee is one cent per $100 of consideration: $436,700 ÷ 100 = 4,367 × $0.01 = $43.67. The buyer pays it by agreement, so it's a buyer debit, and the closing pays it to the clerk and recorder, so it's a cash credit. It isn't owed to the seller, so there's no seller entry.

questions.stem: A Colorado contract leaves both title insurance boxes unchecked. On the worksheet, the premium for the owner's title policy is entered as:
choices: A seller debit and a cash disbursement
A buyer debit and a cash disbursement
A seller credit and a buyer debit
Split equally between buyer and seller debits
questions.explanation: Under the Commission's residential contract, if neither box is checked the seller selects the title company and pays for the owner's policy. It's paid to the title company, so it's a single entry: seller debit, cash credit.

questions.stem: A Colorado sale closes August 20 (not a leap year). Current-year taxes are unpaid and are prorated on last year's bill of $3,650 using a 365-day year; the buyer owns the day of closing. What is the tax entry?
choices: Credit seller $2,310; debit buyer $2,310
Debit seller $2,310; credit buyer $2,310
Debit seller $1,340; credit buyer $1,340
Debit seller $2,342.08; credit buyer $2,342.08
questions.explanation: The seller owned January 1–August 19 = 231 days: $3,650 ÷ 365 × 231 = $2,310. Colorado taxes are paid in arrears, so the buyer will pay this year's whole bill next year; the seller is debited and the buyer credited. $2,342.08 comes from wrongly using a 360-day year ($3,650 ÷ 360 × 231).

questions.stem: A March closing in Colorado. The seller has not yet paid last year's property taxes, which are now due. How are they handled?
choices: Prorated between buyer and seller
Buyer debit, because the buyer will own the property when they're paid
Seller debit for the full amount, paid out to the county treasurer
Seller debit and buyer credit, with no cash entry
questions.explanation: Last year's taxes belong entirely to the seller, who owned the property all of that year. They're paid off at closing: a seller debit and a cash disbursement to the treasurer. Only the current year is prorated.

questions.stem: Price $395,000. The buyer has deposited $10,000 earnest money and gets a new $355,500 loan. The buyer's loan costs and prepaids total $7,200, the documentary fee is charged to the buyer, the buyer reimburses the seller $120 for prepaid HOA dues, and the buyer is credited $1,460 for the seller's share of unpaid taxes. How much cash must the buyer bring to closing?
questions.explanation: Buyer debits: $395,000 + $7,200 + $39.50 doc fee + $120 HOA = $402,359.50. Buyer credits: $10,000 + $355,500 + $1,460 = $366,960. Cash due = $35,399.50. Forgetting the earnest money credit gives $45,399.50.

questions.stem: A Colorado seller's statement shows: price $505,000; loan payoff $268,300; brokerage fee 5.5% of the price; owner's title policy $1,700; half the closing fee $325; tax proration $2,105 (current year unpaid); and a $95 credit for HOA dues the seller prepaid. What is the balance due to the seller?
questions.explanation: Credits: $505,000 + $95 = $505,095. Debits: $268,300 + $27,775 + $1,700 + $325 + $2,105 = $300,205. Balance due to seller = $204,890. The unpaid-tax proration is a seller debit; treating it as a credit overstates the net by $4,210.

questions.stem: After totaling the buyer's columns, the buyer's debits exceed the buyer's credits by $41,250. How is this balance entered to finish the worksheet?
choices: Buyer debit and broker (cash) credit
Seller credit and buyer debit, no cash entry
Buyer credit and broker (cash) debit
Broker (cash) credit only
questions.explanation: The balance due from the buyer is entered as a buyer credit so the buyer's columns balance, and as a cash debit because the closing receives that money from the buyer.

questions.stem: The seller's credits exceed the seller's debits by $96,400. To close out the worksheet, the balance due to the seller is entered as:
choices: Seller credit and broker (cash) debit
Seller debit and broker (cash) credit
Seller debit and buyer credit, no cash entry
Buyer debit and seller credit
questions.explanation: Entering the proceeds as a seller debit brings the seller's columns into balance; the cash column shows it as a credit because the closing pays the money out to the seller.

questions.stem: A buyer assumes a loan with a $210,000 balance at 5.1% interest, paid in arrears. The seller made the payment due on the 1st of the closing month. Closing is on the 17th; use a 30-day month and the buyer owns the day of closing. What is the interest proration?
choices: Debit seller $476; credit buyer $476
Credit seller $476; debit buyer $476
Debit seller $505.75; credit buyer $505.75
Debit seller $892.50; credit buyer $892.50
questions.explanation: Monthly interest = $210,000 × 5.1% ÷ 12 = $892.50; daily = $29.75. The seller owns days 1–16 = 16 days → $476. Interest is paid in arrears, so the buyer's next payment will cover the seller's days; debit the seller and credit the buyer.

questions.stem: A buyer assumes the seller's loan, and the lender's escrow account holding $1,480 for taxes and insurance transfers to the buyer. How is the reserve entered?
choices: Debit seller $1,480; credit buyer $1,480
Credit seller $1,480; debit buyer $1,480
Credit buyer $1,480 and cash debit $1,480
Debit seller $1,480 and cash credit $1,480
questions.explanation: The seller funded the escrow account and the buyer gets the benefit of it, like any prepaid item: credit the seller and debit the buyer. No cash moves at closing.

questions.stem: Price $340,000. The buyer deposited $8,000 earnest money and assumes a loan balance of $196,500. Accrued interest of $420 is prorated (current interest paid in arrears), the buyer reimburses the seller's $1,150 escrow reserve, and the buyer is credited $1,900 for unpaid taxes. The buyer also pays a $750 assumption fee and $310 in other closing costs. What is the balance due from the buyer?
questions.explanation: Buyer debits: $340,000 + $1,150 + $750 + $310 = $342,210. Buyer credits: $8,000 + $196,500 + $420 + $1,900 = $206,820. Balance due = $135,390. The interest is a buyer credit because the buyer will pay it with the next payment.

questions.stem: A seller sells for $310,000 and carries back a $31,000 note. Her loan payoff is $142,000, the brokerage fee is 6% of the price, and her other closing costs and prorations total $2,280 (all debits). How much cash does she receive at closing?
questions.explanation: Debits: $31,000 note + $142,000 + $18,600 fee + $2,280 = $193,880. $310,000 − $193,880 = $116,120. The note reduces cash at closing; she collects it later in payments. The fee is still based on the full price; leaving it out gives $134,720.

questions.stem: Price $280,000. Buyer deposited $7,000 earnest money, gets a new first loan of $224,000, and the seller carries back a $28,000 second. The buyer's loan and closing costs are $6,400, and the buyer is credited $980 for unpaid current-year taxes. What is the buyer's cash due at closing?

A rental home closes September 22. The seller collected September rent of $1,950 and holds a $1,950 security deposit; the lease is assigned to the buyer. Using a 30-day month with the buyer owning the closing day, what are the seller's total debits for these two items?
questions.explanation: Buyer's days: September 22–30 = 9 days; $1,950 ÷ 30 × 9 = $585 (debit seller, credit buyer). The deposit transfers in full, not prorated: another $1,950 debit. Total = $2,535.

questions.stem: A worksheet's cash column shows receipts $1,800 higher than disbursements. Every party column balances. Which mistake best explains this?
choices: The $1,800 tax proration was entered as debit seller, credit buyer
The $1,800 escrow reserve on an assumed loan was left off entirely
The buyer's $1,800 HOA reimbursement was entered as debit buyer, credit seller
The seller's $1,800 owner's title premium was given no cash entry
questions.explanation: A single-entry item paid to an outsider needs both a party debit and a cash credit. Leaving off the disbursement makes receipts exceed payouts by that amount. Double entries between the parties have no cash entry, so handling them correctly can't throw the cash column off.

questions.stem: The contract requires the seller to pay $5,000 toward the buyer's closing costs. On the worksheet, the concession is:
choices: A seller credit and a buyer debit
A seller debit and a buyer credit
A buyer credit and a cash debit
A seller debit and a cash disbursement
questions.explanation: A seller concession moves value from the seller to the buyer: it reduces the seller's proceeds and reduces the cash the buyer must bring. It's a double entry with no cash line of its own.

questions.stem: A Colorado buyer's lender delivers a federal Closing Disclosure. What is the listing broker's obligation regarding the seller's closing statement?
choices: None, since on financed sales the Closing Disclosure replaces the closing statement
Only to hand the seller a copy of the buyer's Closing Disclosure for the file
To see that the seller gets an accurate closing statement signed by the broker
To sign the Closing Disclosure so that it serves as the Colorado closing statement
questions.explanation: The Closing Disclosure is a federal lending form. Commission rules separately make the broker who works with a party responsible for seeing that the party receives an accurate, complete closing statement signed by the broker, and license law requires the buyer and seller to get one; the Closing Disclosure doesn't substitute for it.

questions.stem: Which pair of entries is correct for a Colorado closing?
choices: Current-year property taxes not yet billed: credit seller, debit buyer
Fuel oil the seller paid for and left in the tank: credit seller, debit buyer
Rent the seller collected for the rest of the month: credit seller, debit buyer
Accrued interest on an assumed loan: credit seller, debit buyer
questions.explanation: Items the seller prepaid and the buyer will use (like fuel left in the tank) are credited to the seller. Unpaid taxes, accrued interest and rent already collected for the buyer's days all go the other way: debit seller, credit buyer.

questions.stem: A seller owns a manufactured home that sits on a rented space in a mobile home park. Which Commission-approved contract fits the sale of the home?
choices: Contract to Buy and Sell Real Estate (Residential)
Contract to Buy and Sell Real Estate (Land) with the Manufactured Home Addendum
Manufactured Home Contract to Buy and Sell (Lot Lease Only)
Contract to Buy and Sell Real Estate (Income-Residential)
questions.explanation: When the home sits on a leased lot, no land changes hands, so the Commission's Lot Lease Only manufactured home contract is the form. The Manufactured Home Addendum is for a home that comes with land sold under the Land or Commercial contract.

questions.stem: How does title to the home pass under the Manufactured Home Contract to Buy and Sell (Lot Lease Only)?
choices: By the home's certificate of title; the buyer then applies to the Department of Revenue
By a special warranty deed from the seller, recorded with the county clerk and recorder
By assignment of the lot lease, which carries ownership of the home along with it
By a quitclaim deed from the park owner, recorded in the county where the park is located
questions.explanation: A manufactured home on a leased lot is titled like a vehicle. The seller delivers the certificate of title, and after closing the buyer applies to the Department of Revenue for a new title. No deed is used because no land is conveyed.
