Matters only for firms that manage rentals
Ends the firm's right to list in the MLS
Is excused if the firm uses the logo in its ads
questions.explanation: Failing to display the Equal Housing Opportunity poster can be treated as evidence of discrimination in a fair housing complaint.

questions.stem: An owner lives in one unit of a fourplex and rents the other three herself, with no broker and no discriminatory ads. Which Fair Housing Act exemption may apply?
choices: The single-family home exemption
The housing for older persons (55 and over) exemption
The private club exemption
The owner-occupied (Mrs. Murphy) exemption
questions.explanation: The Mrs. Murphy exemption covers owner-occupied buildings with up to four units. It never covers discriminatory advertising or race discrimination.

questions.stem: A community wants to qualify as "55 and older" housing under the federal Fair Housing Act. Which requirement applies?
choices: Every occupant must be at least 55
At least 80% of occupied units have a resident 55 or older
At least half of all residents must be retired from full-time work
The owner must be a religious organization
questions.explanation: 55-and-older housing needs at least 80% of occupied units to have one resident 55 or older, plus published policies and age verification. It's exempt from the familial status rules only.

questions.stem: A church owns non-commercial housing and limits it to members of its faith. Church membership is open to people of any race. This is:
choices: Allowed only if the church uses a broker
Illegal in every case, because religion is a protected class under the Act
Permitted under the religious organization exemption
Illegal steering by the church
questions.explanation: Religious organizations may limit non-commercial housing they own to their members, unless membership is restricted by race, color or national origin.

questions.stem: Federal Fair Housing Act accessibility design requirements apply to which new construction?
choices: Buildings of 4 or more units first occupied after March 13, 1991
Duplexes first occupied after 1988
Any home a broker lists for sale
Single-family homes built for sale
questions.explanation: New multifamily buildings with 4 or more units first occupied after March 13, 1991 must meet federal accessibility design standards.

questions.stem: Where there is a pattern or practice of housing discrimination, who may bring a federal lawsuit?
choices: The local MLS
Only the state real estate commission
Only the individual victims
The U.S. Attorney General
questions.explanation: The U.S. Attorney General can sue where there's a pattern or practice of discrimination. Individuals can also file with HUD (one year) or sue privately (two years).

questions.stem: A licensee is properly documented as an independent contractor. Who pays her Social Security and Medicare taxes?
choices: The employing broker withholds and pays them
She pays them herself as self-employment tax
The clients pay them through closing costs at settlement
No one, because commissions are exempt
questions.explanation: An independent contractor pays her own self-employment tax. An employer withholds and pays its share only for employees.

questions.stem: A developer tells a buyer, "I'll sell you this lot only if you list your current home with my brokerage." This is:
choices: Price fixing
Market allocation among competitors
A tie-in arrangement
A group boycott
questions.explanation: A tie-in arrangement conditions one product or service on buying another. It's one of the antitrust violations the exam names.

questions.stem: Which statement about commission rates is correct?
choices: A brokerage may set its own commission policy for its listings
Brokers in the same MLS may agree on a minimum commission
Telling sellers "the standard commission is 6%" is good practice
State law sets the commission rate for home sales
questions.explanation: A firm may set its own internal commission policy. The antitrust violation is an agreement among competitors, and calling a rate "standard" implies a fixed rate and should be avoided.

questions.stem: Under federal telemarketing rules, a broker may make permitted cold calls between:
choices: 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. on weekdays only
8 a.m. and 8 p.m. in the caller's time zone
7 a.m. and 10 p.m. in the caller's own home time zone
8 a.m. and 9 p.m. at the called person's location
questions.explanation: Calling hours are 8 a.m. to 9 p.m., local time where the called person is.

questions.stem: A homeowner whose number is on the national Do-Not-Call Registry called a broker two months ago to ask about listing her home. May the broker call her?
choices: No, registry numbers can never be called
Yes, within 3 months of an inquiry the broker may call
Yes, but only between noon and 5 p.m.
Only after she sends a signed written request to be called
questions.explanation: The established business relationship exception allows calls within 3 months after an inquiry or application, or within 18 months after the last purchase or transaction.

questions.stem: A past client asks a brokerage to stop calling her. Under the FCC's telemarketing rules, how long must the firm honor the request on its company-specific do-not-call list?
choices: 31 days
18 months
5 years
Permanently
questions.explanation: FCC rules require a do-not-call request to be honored within a reasonable time (no more than 10 business days) and for 5 years from the request. The 31-day figure is how often you must re-check the national registry; 18 months is the established business relationship window after a transaction.

questions.stem: A broker wants to cold-call FSBO sellers whose numbers are on the national Do-Not-Call Registry, since they're publicly advertising their homes. Which statement is correct?
choices: The registry still applies; public advertising is no exemption
The broker may call if the home is priced over $500,000
FSBO numbers are exempt because the property is publicly advertised
The broker may call each FSBO seller once per listing
questions.explanation: Expired listings and FSBOs aren't exempt from Do-Not-Call rules just because the property is publicly advertised.

questions.stem: A broker wants to send automated marketing texts to a list of cell phone numbers. Under the TCPA, she generally needs:
choices: Approval from the MLS
Only the recipients' oral consent
No consent, since texts aren't calls
Prior express written consent
questions.explanation: Texts count as calls under the TCPA, and autodialed or prerecorded marketing calls and texts need the recipient's prior express written consent.

questions.stem: A brokerage hires a marketing company to send its listing emails. Which statement is correct under the CAN-SPAM Act?
choices: Only the marketing company is responsible for compliance
The emails must include a valid physical postal address
Emails to past clients need no opt-out method
Subject lines may be misleading if the body is accurate
questions.explanation: CAN-SPAM requires a valid physical postal address, an opt-out method and honest headers and subject lines. The brokerage stays responsible even when it hires someone else to send the emails.

questions.stem: A broker wants to advertise another firm's listing on her social media page to generate leads. What must she have first?
choices: Approval from HUD
Nothing, because listings in the MLS are already public information
Permission of the owner and the listing broker
A buyer agency agreement with a buyer
questions.explanation: Don't advertise a property without the owner's permission, and the listing broker's if it's another firm's listing. Online ads follow the same rules as print.

questions.stem: A broker takes earnest money out of the trust account to pay office rent, planning to repay it next week. This is:
choices: Conversion, grounds for license revocation
Acceptable if the amount is under $1,000
A tie-in arrangement
Commingling, which is allowed if the money is repaid promptly
questions.explanation: Using client money for your own purposes is conversion, which is theft and grounds for revocation. Intending to repay doesn't cure it.

questions.stem: A seller says his home is 2,400 square feet. The broker advertises that figure without checking; the home is actually 1,900 square feet, and a buyer relied on the ad. The broker:
choices: Is protected because square footage is opinion
Is liable only if the buyer's lender objects
Isn't liable, because the seller supplied the number
May be liable for negligent misrepresentation
questions.explanation: Due diligence means verifying facts before you repeat them. Passing along a seller's statement as fact without reasonable checking can be negligent misrepresentation.

questions.stem: A team within a brokerage wants to advertise as "The Summit Group." What must its advertising avoid?
choices: Using any name other than the members' legal names
Misleading the public about which firm is the brokerage
Mentioning the employing brokerage at all
Listing more than one team member's contact information
questions.explanation: Teams may market under a team name, but the team isn't the brokerage, and its ads can't mislead the public about who the brokerage is.

questions.stem: A grateful seller wants to hand his broker a $1,000 bonus check directly at closing. The broker should:
choices: Accept it, since it's a gift from the client
Accept it as long as the buyer is told
Have the payment go through her employing broker
Deposit it directly into her personal business checking account
questions.explanation: A licensee can be paid for real estate work only by her own employing broker, not directly by a client or another firm.

questions.stem: A property manager's compensation under a management agreement is most commonly based on:
choices: A percentage of gross rents collected
A percentage of the property's market value
The owner's net profit after taxes
The number of maintenance calls handled
questions.explanation: Management fees are often a percentage of gross rents collected, sometimes plus leasing fees or a flat fee, as set in the management agreement.

questions.stem: Which tenant screening practice is the best fair housing defense?
choices: Accepting the first applicant who offers cash
Letting long-time tenants approve new neighbors
Meeting each applicant in person to judge whether they'll fit in
Applying the same written criteria to every applicant
questions.explanation: Using the same written criteria (income, credit, rental history, references) for every applicant is a property manager's best fair housing defense.

questions.stem: A fire makes an office building unusable for four months while it's repaired. Which coverage replaces the owner's lost rent?
choices: Workers' compensation
Loss of rents insurance
A coinsurance clause
Commercial general liability insurance
questions.explanation: Loss of rents (business interruption) insurance replaces income while damage is repaired. Liability covers injuries to others; workers' compensation covers employees.

questions.stem: An owner's property policy has an 80% coinsurance clause. To collect in full on a partial loss, the owner must:
choices: File claims within 80 days of the loss
Pay 80% of every loss out of pocket
Insure for at least 80% of the property's value
Keep the building at least 80% leased and occupied at all times
questions.explanation: A coinsurance clause requires the owner to carry insurance equal to a stated percentage of value (often 80%) to collect fully on partial losses.

questions.stem: A landlord limits two-bedroom apartments to two occupants total, which in practice bars most families with children. This policy:
choices: Can be familial status discrimination
Is required by the ADA
Is legal if posted in the leasing office
Is always legal, since landlords set occupancy limits
questions.explanation: Occupancy limits must be reasonable and applied equally. A policy that effectively excludes children can be familial status discrimination.

questions.stem: A landlord keeps entering a tenant's apartment without notice when there's no emergency. Which tenant right is the landlord violating?
choices: Constructive eviction
Habitability
Reasonable accommodation
Quiet enjoyment
questions.explanation: Quiet enjoyment is the tenant's right to use the premises without interference by the landlord. The landlord must give reasonable notice before entering except in emergencies.

questions.stem: A residential landlord leaves the building without working plumbing for weeks. In most states, this breaches:
choices: The management agreement
The implied warranty of habitability
The tenant's duty to return the unit in good condition
Title III of the ADA
questions.explanation: Most states impose an implied warranty that residential premises are fit to live in, including working plumbing, heat, water and electrical.

questions.stem: At move-out, a tenant generally must return the rental unit:
choices: In whatever condition it happens to be in on the move-out date
In brand-new condition
In the same condition, less normal wear and tear
Freshly painted at her own cost
questions.explanation: A tenant must return the unit in the same condition it was received, less normal wear and tear.

questions.stem: Compared with residential leases, commercial leases typically:
choices: Have fewer statutory protections, so the written terms control
Must use a state-mandated form lease
Are limited by law to one-year terms
Always require the landlord to pay all property taxes, insurance and maintenance costs
questions.explanation: Commercial leases are treated as deals between business parties, with fewer statutory protections, longer terms and rent often shifting expenses to the tenant. The lease language controls.

questions.stem: A long-term office lease says the rent adjusts each year with the Consumer Price Index. This is a(n):
choices: Percentage lease
Ground lease
Graduated lease
Index lease
questions.explanation: An index (escalation) lease ties rent changes to an index such as the CPI. A graduated lease rises in scheduled steps set in advance.

questions.stem: A retail lease calls for $4,000 a month base rent plus 5% of annual gross sales over $700,000. This year's sales are $900,000. What is the total annual rent?
questions.explanation: Use the stated breakpoint. Base rent is $4,000 × 12 = $48,000. Overage is $900,000 − $700,000 = $200,000 × 5% = $10,000. Total = $58,000.

questions.stem: A landlord offers a $30 per square foot tenant improvement allowance on 2,000 square feet. The tenant's build-out costs $75,000. Who pays what?
choices: The tenant pays $45,000
The tenant pays the full $75,000
The tenant pays $15,000
The landlord pays the full $75,000
questions.explanation: The allowance is 2,000 × $30 = $60,000. The tenant pays the cost above the allowance: $75,000 − $60,000 = $15,000.

questions.stem: A broker sells a sandwich shop's equipment, inventory and goodwill. No real estate is included. The main document that transfers these assets is a:
choices: Bill of sale
General warranty deed
Ground lease
Deed of trust
questions.explanation: A business opportunity sale is mostly personal property, which transfers by a bill of sale. A deed is used only if real estate is included.

questions.stem: A buyer purchases most of a store's inventory and equipment outside the ordinary course of business. Where bulk sale notice rules still exist, they mainly protect:
choices: The store's customers
The landlord and the other tenants in the shopping center
The buyer's lender
The seller's creditors and tax authorities
questions.explanation: Bulk sale laws were designed to protect the seller's creditors and tax authorities through advance notice, so the buyer doesn't inherit unpaid obligations such as taxes.

questions.stem: An owner sold the surface of her ranch but kept the mineral rights. Oil is later found beneath it. Who owns the oil?
choices: The buyer, since surface ownership includes everything below
The original owner, who kept the mineral estate
The state, since minerals are publicly owned
The buyer and seller, split equally by law
questions.explanation: The surface and mineral estates can be severed and sold separately. An owner who sold the surface but kept the minerals still owns the oil and gas below.

questions.stem: Under an oil and gas lease, the periodic payment that keeps the lease alive during the primary term when drilling hasn't started is the:
choices: Bonus
Royalty
Delay rental
Shut-in royalty
questions.explanation: A delay rental keeps the lease in force during the primary term without drilling. The bonus is paid once at signing; a royalty is a share of actual production.

questions.stem: A rancher donates a conservation easement to a land trust that bars subdivision of the ranch. Which statement is correct?
choices: The restriction usually binds future owners
The easement ends when the ranch is sold
Ranching and farming must stop permanently on the property
The rancher gives up ownership of the land
questions.explanation: A conservation easement is a recorded, usually permanent restriction that binds future owners. The owner keeps ownership and can usually keep farming or ranching.

questions.stem: A buyer plans to subdivide land that is currently classified for agricultural use for property tax purposes. What should the broker point out?
choices: Agricultural classification stays with the land permanently
Water rights always transfer automatically with the land
Mineral rights can never be severed from farmland
Changing the use can raise property taxes
questions.explanation: Agricultural use often qualifies land for a lower tax classification, and changing the use can change the tax. Water and mineral rights may be separate from the land.

questions.stem: Several brokers in the same MLS agree to stop showing a competitor's listings, arguing that MLS rules let members set their own showing policies. This is:
choices: Permitted, because MLS membership rules control
A group boycott, despite the MLS rules
Legal if the MLS board approves it
A fair housing violation
questions.explanation: MLS rules can't override antitrust law. Competitors agreeing to refuse to deal with a particular broker is a group boycott.

questions.stem: A listing broker opts out of IDX display for all of her listings. Under typical MLS rules, what usually follows?
choices: The sellers must sign a new listing agreement
Her listings are removed from the MLS entirely
She usually loses the right to display others' listings via IDX
She must pay the MLS a per-listing fee for each listing she enters
questions.explanation: Listing brokers are presumed to allow IDX display unless they opt out. A broker who opts out entirely usually loses the right to display other participants' listings.

questions.stem: Which wording is safest for a home listing ad under fair housing rules?
choices: Three bedrooms near a park
Ideal for empty nesters
Quiet Christian neighborhood
Perfect for young couples
questions.explanation: Describe the property, not the people you want. Phrases about who would suit the home can signal a preference based on familial status, religion or other protected classes.

questions.stem: After HUD withdrew its 2024 guidance on digital ad platforms in 2025, which statement is correct?
choices: Brokers must now get HUD approval before running any online housing ad
Ad targeting is no longer covered by fair housing law
Only print ads remain subject to the Fair Housing Act
The statute and HUD's advertising regulation still apply
questions.explanation: Withdrawing guidance didn't change the Fair Housing Act or HUD's advertising regulation, which still bars choosing where or to whom ads run so as to keep protected groups from learning about housing.

questions.stem: An hour after wiring her down payment, a buyer realizes the emailed instructions were fraudulent. What should she do first?
choices: Wait until the closing appointment to let the title company check
Call her bank right away to request a recall
Send a second wire to the correct account
Email the sender asking for the money back
questions.explanation: Speed matters: call the bank immediately to request a recall, then notify the title company and file a complaint with the FBI's IC3. Funds can sometimes be frozen if reported quickly.

questions.stem: During a showing with a new prospect, which safety practice is recommended?
choices: Meet the prospect at the vacant property first
Park in the driveway behind the prospect's car
Let the prospect walk ahead of you through the home
Lead the prospect into every room, including the basement, first
questions.explanation: Let the prospect walk ahead of you, park on the street so you can't be blocked in, and meet new prospects at the office first.

questions.stem: A property manager collects rents and security deposits for an owner's apartment building under a management agreement. Which statement is correct?
choices: She is a general agent and must hold deposits in a trust account
She is a universal agent with a power of attorney
She is a general agent and may hold deposits in her operating account
She is a special agent, like a listing broker
questions.explanation: A property manager handles an ongoing range of tasks, making her a general agent. Rents and deposits belong to others and go in a trust account, never commingled with her own funds.

questions.stem: Two competing commercial brokerages agree to quote every tenant the same leasing fee of $1.50 per square foot. This is:
choices: A legal co-brokerage agreement
Market allocation
A tie-in arrangement
Price fixing
questions.explanation: Competitors agreeing on fees is price fixing. Co-brokerage agreements set how cooperating brokers split a fee on a deal; they don't let competitors agree on rates.

questions.stem: A landlord approves a tenant's assistance animal in a no-pets building as a disability accommodation, then wants to charge the usual $300 pet deposit. This is:
choices: Allowed, because every animal living in a unit is treated as a pet under the lease
Generally not allowed, since an assistance animal isn't a pet
Required by HUD for all animals
Allowed if the tenant also pays for a modification
questions.explanation: Allowing an assistance animal is a reasonable accommodation, and an assistance animal isn't treated as a pet, so pet rent and pet deposits normally don't apply.

questions.stem: Which body adopts the rules Colorado brokers must follow and makes the final decision in disciplinary cases?
choices: The Division of Real Estate's investigative staff
The Colorado Real Estate Commission
The executive director of the Department of Regulatory Agencies
The Colorado Association of REALTORS
questions.explanation: The Commission is the policy board: it adopts rules, approves forms, and decides discipline and license denials. The Division's staff investigates, audits, and enforces, but doesn't make the final call.

questions.stem: A broker's case has gone to a formal disciplinary hearing. Who conducts the hearing, and what is needed to revoke the license?
choices: An administrative law judge hears it; revocation takes a majority vote of the Commission
The Division director hears it and may revoke the license on his own authority
A district court judge hears it and enters the revocation order directly
A panel of local brokers hears it and sends a recommended penalty to the governor
questions.explanation: Formal hearings are conducted by an administrative law judge under the state Administrative Procedure Act, and no license can be denied, suspended, or revoked except by a majority vote of the Commission.

questions.stem: An unlicensed person keeps advertising homes and negotiating sales for fees. Besides criminal prosecution, what can the Commission do?
choices: Issue a letter of admonition with a $2,500 fine
Nothing, because its authority covers only licensees
Ask a court for an injunction to stop the activity
Order the person's clients to rescind their contracts
questions.explanation: The Commission can seek a court injunction against anyone, licensed or not, who violates the license law. Unlicensed brokerage is also a class 2 misdemeanor.

questions.stem: An associate broker commits a serious violation. The firm's responsible broker had no personal knowledge of it. Can the Commission act against the brokerage firm itself?
choices: No; a firm can be disciplined only if its responsible broker knew of it
Yes; it can suspend or revoke the firm's right to operate either way
No; the Commission may discipline individuals but never firms
Yes, but only with a fine, never a suspension or revocation
questions.explanation: The Commission can suspend or revoke a brokerage firm's right to operate whether or not the firm's responsible broker personally knew of the violation.

questions.stem: A consumer asks the Division for a broker's investigative file in a pending complaint and for a stipulation the broker signed in an earlier case. Which of these is a public record?
choices: Both the investigative file and the stipulation
Only the investigative file
Neither one, because all discipline is confidential
Only the stipulation
questions.explanation: Complaints and investigative files are closed to the public, while stipulations (settlements) and final orders are public records.

questions.stem: Under Colorado law, acting as a real estate broker without a license, or while a license is suspended or revoked, is:
choices: a civil infraction with a small fixed fine
a class 4 felony in every case
handled only by the Commission, with no criminal penalty
a class 2 misdemeanor
questions.explanation: Unlicensed brokerage is a class 2 misdemeanor for individuals and entities alike. The Commission can also seek an injunction.

questions.stem: An associate broker misrepresents a home's condition to a buyer. When can the Commission also discipline the associate's employing broker?
choices: Whenever any associate on the firm's license commits any kind of violation
Only if the employing broker shared in the commission on the sale
If the employing broker knew of it or was negligent in supervising
Never, because each broker answers only for their own conduct
questions.explanation: An employing broker isn't automatically disciplined for an associate's violation. The Commission can act if the employing broker had actual knowledge of it or was negligent in supervising.

questions.stem: Lee holds a power of attorney for his elderly aunt and sells her house for her. Lee has no real estate license. When would Lee need one?
choices: If the sale price is above a set dollar limit
If he accepts compensation for handling the sale
Always, because he is selling property he doesn't own
Never, because a power of attorney replaces a license
questions.explanation: An attorney-in-fact acting under a power of attorney is exempt only when acting without compensation. Taking a fee for the sale would require a license.

questions.stem: A broker has been licensed for six months. Which task is part of the high level of supervision her employing broker must provide?
choices: Reviewing her closing documents in advance
Co-signing each of her listings as seller's agent
Paying her errors and omissions premiums
Attending every showing she schedules
questions.explanation: For brokers with less than two years of experience, the employing broker must give a high level of supervision: training on office policies, availability for consultation, help preparing contracts, monitoring transactions, reviewing closing documents in advance, and making sure an experienced broker attends or is available for closings.

questions.stem: Which applicant may file a Colorado broker license application now?
choices: Age 17; finished 168 hours; passed both portions last month
Age 25; passed both portions 13 months ago; fingerprints on file
Age 30; passed both portions 8 months ago; fingerprints already sent to CBI
Age 22; passed both portions 2 months ago; will send fingerprints after applying
questions.explanation: An applicant must be at least 18, file within one year of passing the exam, and submit fingerprints to the Colorado Bureau of Investigation before applying. Only the 30-year-old meets all three.

questions.stem: A license applicant once pleaded no contest to a misdemeanor and received a deferred judgment. What must the applicant do?
choices: Nothing, because a deferred judgment isn't a conviction
Disclose it only if the offense involved fraud or theft
Disclose it only if the background check turns it up on its own
Disclose it, with court documents and a written explanation
questions.explanation: Applicants must disclose past convictions, pleas including no contest, deferred judgments, and pending charges, and provide court documents and a written explanation.

questions.stem: An associate broker wants to let a friend, an unlicensed investor, do deals under the broker's license and name. Which statement is correct?
choices: It's allowed if the broker reviews each of the friend's deals
It's allowed once the friend completes the 168 hours
It's allowed if the employing broker approves in writing
It's not allowed; a license is personal and can't be lent
questions.explanation: Licenses are personal. They can't be transferred, and a broker can't lend their license or name to anyone else.

questions.stem: How does a Colorado brokerage firm renew its license?
choices: Through its employing or independent broker's renewal
By filing its own separate renewal application every year
By renewing with the Secretary of State
Through each associate broker's renewal
questions.explanation: Brokerage firms don't renew separately; the firm's employing (or independent) broker renews.

questions.stem: A broker is first licensed in March 2026. How many continuing education hours must she complete before her first renewal?
choices: 24 hours, prorated by month
12 hours of approved electives
None
The 4-hour Annual Commission Update only
questions.explanation: A license issued in 2026 expires December 31, 2026, and a license that expires on December 31 of the year it was issued is exempt from CE at that first renewal (C.R.S. 12-10-213(4)). After that, brokers need 24 hours per three-year cycle.

questions.stem: An employing broker's license is revoked. What happens to the licenses of the associate brokers at the firm?
choices: They go inactive until each moves to a new employing broker
They are revoked along with the employing broker's
They stay Active until the end of the renewal cycle
They aren't affected at all, because each broker's license is personal
questions.explanation: When the employing broker's license is suspended, revoked, or expires, the associates' licenses go inactive automatically until they move to a new employing broker.

questions.stem: Associate broker Kim leaves her firm to join another. Which statement is correct?
choices: She may keep working her open deals and just update her record at renewal time
She can't do licensed work until her license transfers to the new firm
Only her former employing broker needs to tell the Commission
She has 30 days after leaving to notify the Commission
questions.explanation: Both the broker and the employing broker must notify the Commission immediately, and the broker can't do licensed work until the license is transferred to the new employing broker. The 30-day window applies to convictions, not employment changes.

questions.stem: Which licensee is exempt from Colorado's errors and omissions insurance requirement?
choices: An Active broker who works only part time
An Active broker who handles only commercial deals
A broker whose license is Inactive
An Active broker in her first year of licensure
questions.explanation: E&O is required for every Active broker. Inactive brokers are exempt, as are attorney-licensees whose malpractice coverage covers their real estate work.

questions.stem: A brokerage firm buys its own firm-wide independent E&O policy. What minimum limits apply?
choices: $100,000 per claim and $300,000 aggregate
$500,000 per claim and $1,500,000 aggregate
$250,000 per claim and $750,000 aggregate
$1,000,000 per claim and aggregate
questions.explanation: A firm-wide independent policy needs at least $1,000,000 per claim and aggregate, with a deductible no higher than $10,000. The $100,000/$300,000 minimums apply to individual coverage.

questions.stem: A broker's license expired four years ago. How can she hold a Colorado license again?
choices: Pay the renewal fee plus a reinstatement fee equal to it
Pay the renewal fee plus half of it as a reinstatement fee
Apply as a new applicant
Pay only the renewal fee if her CE is current
questions.explanation: A license expired more than three years is treated as a new application. Reinstatement with a full reinstatement fee applies between one and three years; the half fee applies from 31 days to one year.

questions.stem: A firm operates under a national franchise's trademark. What must its advertising include?
choices: The franchisor's Colorado license number
An independent-ownership statement
A Commission approval number for the ad
The name of every broker in the office
questions.explanation: When a firm uses a franchise or other third party's trade name or trademark, its ads must include a statement such as "Each office independently owned and operated."

questions.stem: A broker wants to feature a home listed by another firm on her own website. What does she need?
choices: Nothing, as long as the home appears in the MLS
The seller's verbal okay, passed along by a buyer
Prior approval of the ad from the Commission
The listing firm's written permission, with that firm disclosed
questions.explanation: A broker can't advertise another firm's listing without the listing firm's written permission, and the listing firm must be disclosed in the ad.

questions.stem: An employing broker delegates, in writing, supervision of the firm's assistants and bookkeeper to a supervisory broker. Who remains ultimately responsible for that supervision?
choices: The employing broker
The supervisory broker alone
The assistants and bookkeeper themselves
No one, because unlicensed staff need no supervision
questions.explanation: The employing broker must supervise associates and all unlicensed staff. Duties can be delegated in writing to a supervisory broker, but the employing broker stays ultimately responsible.

questions.stem: Which written document must every employing broker adopt and have each associate broker receive and sign?
choices: A personal guaranty of the firm's debts
An office policy manual
A noncompete agreement
A Commission-approved team agreement
questions.explanation: Every employing broker must adopt an office policy manual that each associate receives and signs, covering matters such as how brokers are designated and how confidential information is protected.

questions.stem: A Colorado firm wants to pay a referral fee to a broker licensed only in Ohio who sent it a buyer. Which condition must be met?
choices: The buyer pays the Ohio broker directly at the closing table
The Ohio broker tours Colorado homes with the buyer first
The fee goes through the firm and the Ohio broker does no brokerage here
The Ohio broker negotiates the Colorado purchase contract for the buyer
questions.explanation: A referral fee to a broker licensed elsewhere is allowed only if that broker actually referred the client, lives and keeps an office in the other jurisdiction, does no brokerage work in Colorado, and the payment goes through the Colorado firm.

questions.stem: A brokerage co-owns a title company and refers a buyer to it. When must this affiliated business arrangement first be disclosed to the buyer?
choices: Only on the final settlement statement
Within 30 days after closing
Only if the buyer asks about it
At or before the time of the referral
questions.explanation: An affiliated business arrangement must be disclosed to the consumer when or before the referral is made, in writing to all parties by contract signing, and reported to the Commission.

questions.stem: A broker plans to charge a buyer a separate fee for closing services, in addition to the commission. What does Colorado require?
choices: Nothing, as long as the fee is reasonable
Advance approval of the fee by the Commission
Itemized charges and the written consent of the party charged
Payment directly to the broker outside of closing
questions.explanation: A broker who charges separately for closing services must itemize the charges and get the written consent of the party being charged. Charging for legal document preparation isn't allowed at all.

questions.stem: A broker wants to buy a home she has listed as the seller's agent. Which step does the Commission expect?
choices: Give the seller a right to terminate through closing
Keep representing the seller as seller's agent
Skip written disclosure, because she is now acting as a principal
Get the Commission's written approval first
questions.explanation: The Commission strongly discourages buying your own listing. If it happens, the broker should amend or terminate the listing, disclose in writing, and give the seller a right to terminate through closing.

questions.stem: An associate broker moves to a new firm and wants to take her current listings with her. What is required?
choices: Only written notice to the Commission
The seller's written consent and the old firm's assignment
Only the new employing broker's approval
Nothing, because the listings belong to her
questions.explanation: Listings belong to the firm, not the individual broker. Moving one requires the seller's written consent and the original firm's assignment, or a termination and a new listing.

questions.stem: A seller wants to sell her home through a lease-option. What does the Commission recommend?
choices: Use the Commission-approved lease-option contract
Add the option terms to the Additional Provisions of the sale contract
Have the listing broker draft the option agreement
Involve a Colorado attorney, since there's no approved form
questions.explanation: There's no Commission-approved form for lease-options, lease-purchases, or installment land contracts. The Commission strongly urges using a Colorado attorney and recommends separate legal advice for each party.

questions.stem: A buyer gives a promissory note as earnest money, and the note isn't paid when due. What must the broker do?
choices: Cover the amount from the firm's trust account
Cancel the contract on the seller's behalf
Promptly notify the seller and deliver the original note
Wait until closing to tell the seller
questions.explanation: When a promissory note is used as earnest money, the seller must be told its due date; if it isn't paid, the broker must promptly notify the seller and deliver the original note.

questions.stem: An unlicensed, salaried on-site manager handles an apartment complex through a brokerage. Which task may the manager perform?
choices: Quote the rents the owner has set
Negotiate a lower rent and longer term with an applicant
Earn a commission on each lease signed
Change material lease terms at a tenant's request
questions.explanation: Unlicensed on-site managers may fill in lease blanks, show units, quote set rents, arrange maintenance, and collect rents and deposits, but can't negotiate material lease terms. They're paid salary or non-commission income.

questions.stem: Which act is a ground for discipline under Colorado's license law?
choices: Declining a listing the broker isn't competent to handle
Acting for more than one party without everyone's knowledge
Rebating part of the commission to a client with lender approval
Recommending that a buyer have an attorney review title exceptions
questions.explanation: Acting for more than one party without the knowledge of all parties is a listed ground for discipline. Declining work outside your competency, disclosed rebates, and referring title questions to an attorney are what the rules expect.

questions.stem: An independent broker's license is suspended. Within what time must she account for and disburse the trust money she holds?
choices: 7 days
10 days
180 days
30 days
questions.explanation: An independent or employing broker whose license is suspended, revoked, expired, or inactive must account for and disburse trust money within 30 days and give the Commission a list of affected consumers within 7 days.

questions.stem: Under a desk-fee (100%) arrangement, how is a broker's commission handled?
choices: Paid by the client straight to the broker, bypassing the firm entirely
Paid to the firm; the broker keeps most of it after a fixed fee
Split by a percentage that improves as production grows
Paid to the firm, which ends its duty to supervise the broker
questions.explanation: In a desk-fee model the broker pays the firm a fixed monthly or per-transaction fee and keeps most or all of each commission, but the commission is still paid to the firm and supervision duties don't change. A graduated percentage describes a commission split.

questions.stem: A member of a team wants to buy a property the team has listed. What does the Commission's guidance call for?
choices: Commission approval before any offer is written
The buying member stays on the listing as seller's agent
Both parties' written consent to transaction-brokerage, plus a firewall around the buyer
Nothing special, because team members are all principals
questions.explanation: Commission Position CP-16 says the team should get written informed consent from both parties to act as a transaction-broker, remove the buying broker from the listing contract, and firewall that broker from the transaction. No Commission approval is required.

questions.stem: A broker owns and manages a rental house. How can she properly disclose her license status to a tenant?
choices: Calling herself a "licensed landlord" in the lease
Telling the tenant orally at the showing
None is needed, since it's her own property
A written lease statement that she's an owner and a licensed broker
questions.explanation: A broker acting as a principal must disclose license status in writing. For a rental she owns and manages, a lease statement that plainly says she is both an owner and a licensed Colorado real estate broker works; "licensed landlord" isn't enough.

questions.stem: In Colorado, when does a single agency relationship, such as buyer agency, exist?
choices: Once the broker has shown the buyer a property
When the buyer orally asks the broker to represent him
Only under a written agreement signed before brokerage activities
When the seller accepts an offer the broker wrote for the buyer
questions.explanation: Single agency requires a written agreement with the represented party, signed before the broker begins brokerage activities for that party. Without one, the broker is presumed to be a transaction-broker.

questions.stem: A Colorado seller's agent wants other MLS brokers to act as subagents of her seller. Which statement is correct?
choices: It's allowed as long as the seller consents to it in writing
Not allowed; she may cooperate with them but not create subagents
It's allowed only for brokers who work in the same firm
It's required for every listing entered in the MLS
questions.explanation: A Colorado single agent may cooperate with other brokers but may not engage or create subagents. Old-style MLS subagency is not available in Colorado, even with the seller's consent.

questions.stem: A seller's agent is about to work with an unrepresented buyer. Before engaging in brokerage activities with the buyer, the broker's written disclosure must state that:
choices: the buyer will be vicariously liable for the broker's acts
the broker will keep the buyer's price limit confidential
the broker will act as a transaction-broker for the buyer
the broker is the seller's agent and not the buyer's agent
questions.explanation: A seller's agent working with a buyer must disclose in writing that the broker is the seller's agent and not the buyer's, list the tasks the broker will do for the seller, and state that the buyer is not vicariously liable for the agent's acts.

questions.stem: A buyer refuses to sign the acknowledgment on a Brokerage Disclosure to Buyer form. What should the broker do?
choices: Stop working with the buyer, since the form is a required contract
Note the refusal and date on a copy and keep that copy
Ask the employing broker to sign the form on the buyer's behalf
Send the unsigned form to the Division within 3 business days
questions.explanation: The acknowledgment is a receipt, not a contract, so the buyer's refusal doesn't end the relationship. The broker records the refusal and the date on a copy and keeps it (with the delivery email if sent electronically).

questions.stem: A firm's written office policy offers only transaction-brokerage. A buyer asks the broker about buyer agency. What must the broker do?
choices: Give the buyer the Commission's written definition of buyer agency
Refer the buyer to the Division of Real Estate for an explanation
Nothing, because the firm doesn't offer buyer agency
Act as the buyer's agent anyway, since the buyer requested it in person
questions.explanation: A firm need not offer every relationship, but if a party asks about one the firm doesn't offer, the broker must provide the Commission's written definition of it, which is what the Definitions of Working Relationships form is for.

questions.stem: Three brokers at one firm work as a team on a seller's listing. Which statement is correct?
choices: Only the team leader must be designated; others may assist as needed
Members may serve the seller in different capacities if the seller agrees
Every member must be designated in the same capacity and named in the listing
Using a team makes the entire firm the seller's agent for the listing
questions.explanation: Commission rules require every team member to be a designated broker for the consumer in the same capacity, and all members must be named in the listing contract. Designation never extends the relationship to the whole firm.

questions.stem: Which statement about a Colorado employing broker in a firm that uses designated brokerage is correct?
choices: Designating brokers ends the employing broker's duty to supervise them
The firm needs a written policy on which relationships it offers
Clients become vicariously liable for acts of the brokers they hire
The employing broker may never be the designated broker in a transaction
questions.explanation: The employing broker must adopt a written office policy describing the relationships offered, how brokers are designated and how confidential information is protected. Designation doesn't reduce the duty to supervise, and the employing broker may be a designated broker.

questions.stem: Under Colorado's brokerage relationships statute, a relationship that is not completed ends at the earliest of the agreed expiration date, termination by the parties, or:
choices: 90 days after it began
two years after it began
the end of the broker's license period
one year after it began
questions.explanation: If the engagement isn't completed, the relationship ends at the earliest of its expiration date, termination by the parties, or one year after it began.

questions.stem: A seller's property is under contract. Her listing broker, a seller's agent, receives another written offer. What must the broker do?
choices: Hold it until the current contract terminates
Present it to the seller in a timely manner
Return it, since property under contract can't receive offers
Present it only if it beats the current contract price
questions.explanation: A single agent must present all offers to and from the client in a timely manner, even when the property is already under contract. What the agent need not do is go looking for more offers while it's under contract.

questions.stem: A buyer's agent's client is about to make an offer on a home. Another of the agent's buyer clients wants to make an offer on the same home. Under Colorado law, the agent:
choices: may help both buyers try to buy it without breaching a duty
must drop one buyer, since helping both breaches loyalty
must become a transaction-broker for both buyers
needs the seller's written consent to help the second buyer
questions.explanation: Colorado's statute says a buyer's agent may show the same property to competing buyers and help them try to buy it; this is not a breach of duty to the first buyer.

questions.stem: A seller pays the fee of a broker who worked with the buyer. Does the payment make the broker the seller's agent?
choices: Yes, a broker is always the agent of the party who pays
Yes, unless the buyer signed a written agreement first
No; payment alone doesn't create an agency relationship
No, because only buyers may pay a buyer's broker in Colorado
questions.explanation: Colorado separates who pays from who is represented: compensation may come from either party or a third party, and paying a broker does not, by itself, create agency.

questions.stem: A homeowner wants a broker to start marketing her home but refuses to sign any listing contract. What is the broker's position?
choices: The broker may market it as a transaction-broker without a listing
The broker may proceed on an oral listing if a witness is present
The broker may proceed after giving her a Brokerage Disclosure form
The broker may not perform brokerage services for her
questions.explanation: A seller or landlord listing must be in writing before any brokerage services are performed, whatever the relationship. If the seller refuses to sign, the broker can't provide brokerage services to her.

questions.stem: Under the Exclusive Right-to-Buy contract, the buyer's brokerage is paid partly from the seller's side and the buyer owes the rest. When does the buyer owe an unpaid balance?
choices: Only if disclosed in writing before the buyer signs the purchase contract
Whenever the seller side pays less, regardless of when it was disclosed
Only if the seller's agent agrees in writing to the buyer paying it
Only if the closing company approves the amount at closing
questions.explanation: Under the 2026 Exclusive Right-to-Buy form, the buyer owes the portion of the fee the seller side doesn't pay only if the broker disclosed the amount to the buyer in writing before the buyer entered into a contract with the seller. Neither the seller's agent nor the closing company can create that obligation.

questions.stem: A residential buyer is offered an engagement contract that would record a lien against her future home to secure the broker's fee. Under C.R.S. 12-10-403.5:
choices: the lien is valid once the contract is recorded with the county
the lien is valid only if the buyer initials that paragraph
the lien is void only if the contract runs longer than one year
it's void, and offering it is a deceptive trade practice
questions.explanation: A residential engagement contract may not create a lien, encumbrance or other recordable interest in the property; any such interest is void, and offering a contract with that term is a deceptive trade practice.

questions.stem: A broker wants to put earnest money in a 12-month certificate of deposit at the trust account bank. Without a written agreement of the parties, this is:
choices: allowed if the CD is titled in the firm's name as a trust account
allowed as long as the broker agrees to pay any withdrawal penalty
not allowed; trust funds must be available at once without penalty
allowed only for earnest money held longer than 30 days
questions.explanation: Trust funds must be available immediately without penalty, so CDs and other fixed-term investments aren't allowed unless the parties agree otherwise in writing.

questions.stem: A Colorado sales firm never holds earnest money because title companies always hold it. How many trust accounts must it maintain?
choices: None; a firm that holds no one else's money may have zero
At least one, titled as a sales escrow account
Two: one for earnest money and one for security deposits
One for each associate broker in the firm
questions.explanation: A firm may have any number of trust accounts, including zero, if it never receives money belonging to others.

questions.stem: A firm's trust account earns interest, and no written agreement says who gets it. Under the Commission's position, the interest:
choices: belongs to the firm as the account holder
is split equally between the firm and the beneficiaries
doesn't belong to the brokerage firm
must be sent to the State Treasurer every month
questions.explanation: Absent a specific written agreement, interest on a trust account does not belong to the firm; keeping it would be undisclosed compensation. The contract, management agreement or lease should say who gets it.

questions.stem: A seller accepts a buyer's promissory note as earnest money. The note isn't paid when due. What must the broker do?
choices: Promptly tell the seller and give the seller the original note
Keep the note in the firm's file and wait for the closing date
Cancel the contract for the seller and return the note to the buyer
Cover the amount with firm funds and collect from the buyer later
questions.explanation: When a note is accepted as earnest money, the seller must be told when it's due; if it isn't paid then, the broker must promptly notify the seller and deliver the original note to the seller.

questions.stem: After a contract terminates, the buyer authorizes in writing that the earnest money go to the seller. The holding brokerage:
choices: must first get the seller's signature on a release as well
may require both parties to sign a release holding the firm harmless
should disburse it as directed without unnecessary delay
must wait for a court order before releasing the money
questions.explanation: When the parties agree, the holder disburses as directed without delay; one party's written authorization in favor of the other is enough. The firm may not demand a hold-harmless or liability-waiver release.

questions.stem: Which deposit of a firm's own money into its trust account is permitted?
choices: A standing cushion of firm money so trust checks never bounce
Earned commissions left in the account until year-end
The employing broker's personal savings, to shield them from creditors
Funds to cover the account's bank charges, recorded in the records
questions.explanation: A firm may deposit its own money to cover bank charges (or a recorded, labeled advance for a client). A cushion, or earned fees left in the account, is commingling; earned fees must be withdrawn monthly.

questions.stem: Management of a rental property moves from Firm A to Firm B. Which deadlines apply to the tenants' security deposits?
choices: B discloses their status within 10 days; A transfers them within 30 days
B discloses their status within 30 days; A transfers them within 60 days
A transfers them within 5 business days; no written disclosure is needed
A refunds the tenants, who then pay new deposits to Firm B
questions.explanation: Commission rules give the new firm 30 days after the management agreement is signed or assigned to disclose the deposits' status in writing to the owner and tenant, and the prior firm 60 days to transfer the deposits to the new firm. Refunding and re-collecting deposits isn't the procedure.

questions.stem: A property management agreement says nothing about owner reports. When are reports to the owner due?
choices: Within 30 days after the end of the month funds were received or paid
Within 10 business days after each tenant's rent payment arrives
Once a year, by January 31 for the prior calendar year
Only when the owner asks for a report in writing
questions.explanation: Reports follow the management agreement; if it's silent, Commission rules require them within 30 days after the end of the month in which funds were received or disbursed. The other timeframes aren't in the rules.

questions.stem: Which item is part of the trust account records a Colorado firm must keep?
choices: A copy of each party's credit report and tax return
Annual financial statements audited by an outside CPA firm
A monthly balance report filed with the Division of Real Estate
Written accounting control policies for people who handle money
questions.explanation: Required trust records include the journal, beneficiary ledgers, monthly three-way reconciliations, bank statements, signed deposit agreements, and written accounting control policies describing checks and balances over people who handle money.

questions.stem: Which written office policy must a Colorado employing broker have concerning records?
choices: A policy for disposing of documents with personal identifying info
A policy requiring all emails and texts to be kept for ten years
A policy for filing every transaction file with the Commission at closing
A policy requiring paper copies of all electronic records
questions.explanation: The employing broker's office policies must include a written policy for disposing of documents containing personal identifying information. Keeping emails and texts is recommended, not required, and electronic records are allowed.

questions.stem: In a Colorado disciplinary matter, which statement correctly describes the roles?
choices: The Commission investigates and the Division decides the discipline
The Division investigates and the Commission decides the discipline
The Attorney General's office both investigates and decides
Local REALTOR boards investigate and the Division decides
questions.explanation: The Division of Real Estate investigates; the Colorado Real Estate Commission decides whether a violation occurred and what discipline fits.

questions.stem: A broker who settled a disciplinary case agreed to follow-up audits of her firm. How was the firm selected for these audits?
choices: At random
By MLS referral
At license renewal
By stipulation
questions.explanation: The Division selects firms for audit randomly, by stipulation (a settlement in which the broker agrees to follow-up audits), or as a result of a complaint or investigation.

questions.stem: A seller files a complaint asking the Division to interpret a contract clause in her favor and make the buyer's broker repay her losses. What is the likely result?
choices: The Commission orders the broker to reimburse her for the losses
The Division interprets the contract clause and then enforces it
Dismissal; contract disputes and money claims are civil matters
The complaint goes to an administrative law judge for a ruling
questions.explanation: Staff first check jurisdiction. Interpreting or enforcing a contract is a civil matter for an attorney or the courts, and Commission discipline isn't a way to collect money from a broker.

questions.stem: Which of these is a public record?
choices: A pending complaint filed against a broker with the Division
The investigator's file on an open investigation
A stipulation settling a disciplinary case
The name of a complainant who filed anonymously
questions.explanation: Complaints and investigation files are closed to the public. Stipulations and final agency orders are public records.

questions.stem: A disciplinary case against a broker does not settle. Who conducts the hearing?
choices: The full Real Estate Commission
The Division director
A district court jury
An administrative law judge
questions.explanation: An administrative law judge from the Office of Administrative Courts hears the case under the state Administrative Procedure Act; the Commission then decides by majority vote, and the Court of Appeals reviews.

questions.stem: Broker A, a designated seller's agent, knows his seller would accept $15,000 less. Broker B, at the same firm, is the designated buyer's agent for a buyer interested in the home. Which is correct?
choices: B is presumed to know it, since both brokers work for the same firm
A can't reveal it without the seller's consent; B isn't charged with knowing it
A must tell B, because the employing broker is now a dual agent
A must disclose it, since the price is an adverse material fact
questions.explanation: A seller's agent may not disclose that the seller would accept less without the seller's informed consent. With designated brokerage, A's knowledge isn't imputed to B, and two designated agents on opposite sides isn't dual agency.

questions.stem: A firm holds the earnest money on a sale that closes. Which trust records must it keep, and for how long?
choices: Only the bank statements, for 3 years after the deposit
Journal and ledgers only, for 5 years from opening the file
Only the closing statement, for 4 years from the listing date
Journal, ledgers and reconciliations, for 4 years from closing
questions.explanation: Each trust account needs a journal, beneficiary ledgers and monthly three-way reconciliation reports, and required records are kept four years from closing (or from listing expiration if it never closed).

questions.stem: A broker has no written agreement with a buyer and has given the transaction-broker disclosure. The buyer says she'd pay $10,000 more than her offer. May the broker tell the seller?
choices: Yes, since a transaction-broker is not the buyer's agent
Yes, as long as the seller asks the broker about it directly
Not without the informed consent of all parties
No, because without a written agreement the broker is the buyer's agent
questions.explanation: Without a written single-agency agreement the broker is a presumed transaction-broker, and a transaction-broker may not disclose that a buyer would pay more without the informed consent of all parties.

questions.stem: A broker's neighbor is selling a cabin to a friend with no broker involved. The neighbor asks the broker to fill in the deed and offers $150 for the paperwork. What should the broker do?
choices: Accept, as long as the broker uses a Commission-approved form
Accept without the fee, so the work falls under the Conway-Bogue conditions
Decline, because the broker isn't brokering this transaction
Accept if both parties sign a written consent to the broker's help
questions.explanation: Brokers may complete standard forms only in transactions where they are acting as the broker, and never for a separate fee. Preparing a deed for someone else's private sale is the unauthorized practice of law, even without a fee or with the parties' consent.

questions.stem: A commercial buyer wants to send a letter of intent before negotiating a full contract. If the broker completes the letter of intent as a standard form, what must it say on its face?
choices: That it becomes binding once both parties sign it
That it replaces any Commission-approved contract for the deal
That the broker drafted it with help from the firm's attorney
That it is nonbinding
questions.explanation: A letter of intent is one of the standard forms a broker may complete, but it must state on its face that it is nonbinding. The binding agreement still goes on the appropriate contract form.

questions.stem: A buyer's broker is helping a client buy a new home, and the builder insists on using its own purchase contract. What must the broker do?
choices: Rewrite the builder's contract to match the Commission-approved residential contract
Advise the buyer in writing to get legal advice from an attorney before signing
Refuse to proceed, because only Commission-approved contracts may be used
Attach the Commission-approved contract as an addendum that overrides the builder's form
questions.explanation: A broker may work with a principal-supplied contract, such as a builder's, by inserting transaction-specific information, but Commission rules require advising the client in writing to consult an attorney before signing. The broker doesn't rewrite or override the principal's form.

questions.stem: A section of a Commission-approved contract doesn't apply to the transaction. How should the broker handle it?
choices: Keep the section caption and mark the text as omitted or not applicable
Delete the whole section, including its caption, so the printed form is shorter
Erase the section and retype the remaining paragraphs in order
Leave it unchanged and tell the parties orally to ignore it
questions.explanation: When a section doesn't apply, its caption stays and the text is marked as omitted or not applicable. Printed text is never erased, and the broker must explain every change to the principal.

questions.stem: A listing broker who is not a party to the sale wants to add a sentence to Additional Provisions stating that neither brokerage is liable for the condition of the roof. May the broker do this?
choices: Yes, because Additional Provisions are not Commission-approved language anyway
Yes, if the seller initials the sentence
Yes, as long as the buyer's broker agrees to it in writing
No; a broker who isn't a party may not add a clause protecting the broker
questions.explanation: Commission rules bar a broker who isn't a party from adding an exculpatory clause that protects the broker. Additional Provisions are for recording what the parties agreed to, not for shielding the broker.

questions.stem: A landlord client asks his broker to use the Commission-approved residential lease. What is accurate?
choices: The broker must use the Income-Residential contract's lease addendum
The Commission has no approved leases or property management agreements
The broker may draft a lease because leasing isn't the practice of law
The Commission's lease is required whenever the broker manages the property
questions.explanation: There are no Commission-approved leases or property management agreements. The lease has to come from another permitted source, such as an attorney-drafted form or one the owner supplies; the broker never drafts it.

questions.stem: A new version of a Commission-approved form became mandatory on January 1. On January 10, a broker's transaction software still fills in the old version. What is the issue?
choices: None, because the old version stays valid until the date printed on it
None, as long as both parties initial each page of the old version
It violates the requirement to use the Commission-approved form
The broker must get the Commission's permission before using the old version
questions.explanation: Each revision has a mandatory-use date. Using an outdated version after its replacement becomes mandatory violates the requirement to use the Commission-approved form, so brokers must make sure their software has the current version.

questions.stem: A buyer's broker fills in the property section of the residential contract with only the street address. What is missing?
choices: Nothing, because a street address fully identifies the property
The county assessor's parcel number, which replaces the address
A new survey, which must be attached to identify the property
The legal description, which an address alone can't replace
questions.explanation: The contract identifies the property by its legal description. A street address alone isn't enough to identify real property for a sale.

questions.stem: The home has leased solar panels. Under the residential contract, what is needed for the panel lease to carry over to the buyer?
choices: Buyer's choice to assume it, plus the lessor's written approval
Nothing, because attached items are automatically included in the sale
A bill of sale from the seller listing the panels as personal property
The listing broker's written confirmation that the lease is transferable
questions.explanation: Leased items and encumbered inclusions require the buyer to choose whether to assume the obligation, plus written approval from the lessor or lienholder before closing. Leased panels belong to the lessor, so a bill of sale from the seller can't convey them.

questions.stem: A home sale includes deeded water rights and shares of water stock. How does the residential contract handle them?
choices: They pass automatically with the deed, so the contract doesn't mention them
They have their own subsection and a Water Rights Examination Deadline
They must be sold under a separate Land contract
They are listed as exclusions and conveyed after closing
questions.explanation: Water rights, including deeded rights, well rights and water stock, have their own subsection in the residential contract and a Water Rights Examination Deadline for the buyer's review.

questions.stem: In the residential contract's purchase price section, what is a seller concession?
choices: A cut in the purchase price that the seller agrees to after a low appraisal
Earnest money the seller agrees to refund if the loan is denied
A credit to the buyer at closing that can cover costs the lender allows
A payment from the seller to the buyer's brokerage firm
questions.explanation: A seller concession is a credit from the seller to the buyer at closing that can cover costs the buyer's lender allows. It isn't a price reduction or compensation to a brokerage.

questions.stem: Under the residential contract, when does the buyer deliver the earnest money if no Alternative Earnest Money Deadline is set?
choices: Within 3 days after the New Loan Application Deadline
At closing, to the closing company
After the Inspection Resolution Deadline passes
With the contract
questions.explanation: The buyer delivers earnest money with the contract unless the parties set an Alternative Earnest Money Deadline. The Earnest Money Holder keeps it in trust for both parties and may transfer it to the closing company at or before closing.

questions.stem: The parties write "N/A" next to the Appraisal Deadline in the Dates and Deadlines table. What is the effect?
choices: That deadline and the provision tied to it don't apply
The deadline defaults to MEC plus 10 days
The deadline becomes the same as the Closing Date
The contract isn't binding until the parties fill in a date
questions.explanation: A deadline left blank or marked N/A or Deleted means that deadline and the provision tied to it don't apply. It doesn't default to another date or keep the contract from forming.

questions.stem: A buyer's offer has an Acceptance Deadline of 8:00 p.m. Friday. The seller signs at 7:30 p.m. Friday, but neither the buyer nor the buyer's broker learns of the signature until Saturday morning. What is the result?
choices: A contract formed at 7:30 p.m., when the seller signed
The offer expired without timely notice of acceptance
A contract formed, because the seller signed before the deadline
The deadline extends automatically to the next business day
questions.explanation: An offer expires unless both parties sign and the offering party receives notice of acceptance by the Acceptance Deadline. Signing alone isn't enough.

questions.stem: The seller will carry back part of the price. Under the residential contract, who may terminate if the financing documents are unsatisfactory?
choices: Only the buyer, by the New Loan Terms Deadline
Only the seller, by the Disapproval of Buyer's Credit Information Deadline
Either party, by the Seller or Private Financing Deadline
Neither party, because seller financing isn't a contingency
questions.explanation: Under the seller or private financing provision, either party may terminate if the financing documents are unsatisfactory in that party's sole subjective discretion, by the Seller or Private Financing Deadline.

questions.stem: The buyer delivers a timely objection to a low appraisal. The seller won't lower the price, nothing is agreed by the Appraisal Resolution Deadline, and the buyer hasn't withdrawn the objection. What happens?
choices: The buyer must close at the contract price
The seller must lower the price to the appraised value
The buyer gets 10 more days to obtain a second appraisal
The contract terminates
questions.explanation: An unresolved appraisal objection terminates the contract at the Appraisal Resolution Deadline unless the buyer withdraws the objection in writing before then. The seller isn't required to cut the price.

questions.stem: A new Improvement Location Certificate shows the garage sits over the setback line. What may the buyer do under the residential contract?
choices: Terminate or object by the New ILC or New Survey Objection Deadline
Nothing, because survey and ILC matters are handled only by the title insurance policy
Require the seller to move the garage before closing
Delay closing until the county grants a variance
questions.explanation: The buyer may terminate or object over an unsatisfactory ILC or survey by the New ILC or New Survey Objection Deadline. If an objection isn't resolved, the contract terminates unless the buyer withdraws it.

questions.stem: Which home requires the lead-based paint disclosure in a Colorado residential sale?
choices: A home built in 1985 with its original exterior paint
Any home with a basement, regardless of its age
A home whose building permit was issued in 1976
A home built in 1990 that was repainted last year
questions.explanation: Lead-based paint disclosure applies to dwellings built, or with a building permit issued, before January 1, 1978. A 1976 permit qualifies.

questions.stem: A seller knows methamphetamine was once manufactured in the home, and the property was never remediated to state standards. What does the residential contract require?
choices: Nothing, because the buyer's inspection will reveal it
The seller must disclose it
The broker must report it to the Real Estate Commission
The seller may disclose it only with the buyer's written consent
questions.explanation: The seller must disclose known methamphetamine manufacture, use or storage unless the property was remediated to state standards. It isn't left to the buyer's inspection.

questions.stem: What does the residential contract say about radon?
choices: The seller must have the home tested for radon before it is listed for sale
The buyer waives radon claims by closing
Radon is covered only in the Commercial contract
It recommends a test; the seller gives known results
questions.explanation: The contract includes a state health department advisory strongly recommending a radon test before buying, and the seller must provide any radon test results the seller knows of. It doesn't require the seller to test.

questions.stem: A home has a gas furnace and bedrooms. Under Colorado law, where must an operational carbon monoxide alarm be installed?
choices: Within 15 feet of each bedroom entrance
Within 5 feet of the furnace or other fuel-fired appliance
Inside the attached garage, near the door to the house
In the main hallway, at least 30 feet from any bedroom
questions.explanation: When a home has a fuel-fired heater or appliance, a fireplace or an attached garage, plus a bedroom, Colorado law requires an operational carbon monoxide alarm within 15 feet of each bedroom entrance (or where the building code requires).

questions.stem: Under the residential contract's source of water provision, what does the buyer acknowledge when the home is served by a well?
choices: That the State Engineer has inspected the well
That the seller warrants the well's water quality
Receiving the water source information and well permit information
That the buyer will apply for a new well permit before the closing date
questions.explanation: The buyer acknowledges receiving the source-of-water information and, for a well, the well permit information. The seller doesn't warrant water quality.

questions.stem: The buyer's inspector damages a deck railing during the inspection, and the buyer later terminates the contract. Who is responsible for the damage?
choices: The seller, because the contract terminated
The buyer, whose obligation survives termination
The listing broker, who allowed the inspection
No one, because inspections are at the seller's risk
questions.explanation: The buyer pays for inspections, must repair damage they cause and indemnifies the seller. Those obligations survive termination of the contract.

questions.stem: A contract is conditioned on the sale of the buyer's current home. That home hasn't sold, and the Conditional Sale Deadline passes with no notice from the buyer. What is the result?
choices: The contract terminates automatically and the earnest money is returned
The deadline extends until the buyer's home sells
The seller must accept a new closing date
The buyer has lost the right to terminate under that contingency
questions.explanation: A buyer with a conditional sale contingency must terminate by the Conditional Sale Deadline or lose that right. Time is of the essence, so the deadline doesn't extend on its own.

questions.stem: Closing has occurred, but the seller doesn't deliver possession at the Possession Date and Time. No occupancy agreement was signed. What does the residential contract provide?
choices: The closing is unwound and the deed goes back to the seller
The buyer must wait 30 days before taking any action
Eviction, plus the contract's per-day amount and damages
The buyer's only remedy is to keep the earnest money
questions.explanation: A seller who holds over after the Possession Date and Time is subject to eviction and owes the per-day amount set in the contract plus actual damages. A seller who plans to stay should sign a Post-Closing Occupancy Agreement.

questions.stem: Before closing, a fire damages a home under contract for $500,000. Repairs are estimated at $65,000. What right does the buyer have?
choices: The buyer may terminate, because the damage exceeds 10% of the price
None, because the seller's homeowner's insurance will cover the repair costs
The buyer may demand a $65,000 price reduction
The buyer must close and file an insurance claim
questions.explanation: If casualty damage exceeds 10% of the purchase price, or the property isn't repaired by the Closing Date, the buyer may terminate. $65,000 is 13% of $500,000.

questions.stem: After closing, the actual property tax bill turns out higher than the figure used to prorate taxes. Additional Provisions say nothing about it. What is the result?
choices: The seller must pay the difference when the bill arrives
The closing company re-prorates using the actual bill
The buyer and seller split the difference equally
The proration stands, because prorations are final
questions.explanation: Under the residential contract, prorations are final unless the Additional Provisions say otherwise, so neither party owes an adjustment after closing.

questions.stem: The buyer terminates by a timely Notice to Terminate under the inspection provision. The buyer isn't in default. What happens to the earnest money?
choices: The seller keeps it as liquidated damages
It is returned to the buyer
It is split equally between buyer and seller
It goes to the listing brokerage as compensation
questions.explanation: When the contract terminates, the earnest money goes back to the buyer unless the buyer is in default. A proper, timely termination isn't a default.

questions.stem: In a Counterproposal, the seller changes the price and leaves the Closing Date line blank. What happens to the Closing Date?
choices: It is deleted and must be renegotiated
It defaults to 30 days after acceptance
It stays as in the proposed contract
The seller may choose it later
questions.explanation: In the Counterproposal tables, a blank or "No Change" leaves the term as it was in the proposed contract, and "Deleted" removes the provision. All other terms stay the same.

questions.stem: A buyer uses the Extension or Termination of Contract form to ask for more time. The seller doesn't sign Part I, and the time for acceptance passes. What is the effect of Part II?
